env.ReadFile(\"fileB.go\")\n\tassert.Contains(t, contentB, \"modified by agent\", \"fileB.go should have agent changes after stash pop\")\n\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Update fileB\", \"fileB.go\")\n\tcheckpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\n\t// Both commits should have checkpoints\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, \"Second commit should have checkpoint\")\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, \"Checkpoints should be different\")\n\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint 1: %s, Checkpoint 2: %s\", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)\n}\n\n// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits tests user splitting agent's modifications\n// to multiple existing files into separate commits.\nfunc TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\n\tenv := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, \"manual-commit\")\n\n\t// Create and commit multiple existing files\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"model.go\", \"package main\\n\\ntype Model struct{}\\n\")\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"view.go\", \"package main\\n\\ntype View struct{}\\n\")\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"controller.go\", \"package main\\n\\ntype Controller struct{}\\n\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add MVC scaffolding\", \"model.go\", \"view.go\", \"controller.go\")\n\n\t// Agent modifies all three files\n\tt.Log(\"Agent modifying model.go, view.go, controller.go\")\n\tprompt := `Add a Name field (string type) to each struct in these files:\n1. model.go - add Name string to Model struct\n2. view.go - add Name string to View struct\n3. controller.go - add Name string to Controller struct\nOnly modify these three files.`\n\n\tresult, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\t// User commits each file separately\n\tt.Log(\"Committing model.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add Name to Model\", \"model.go\")\n\tcheckpointModel := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpointModel, \"Model commit should have checkpoint\")\n\n\tt.Log(\"Committing view.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add Name to View\", \"view.go\")\n\tcheckpointView := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpointView, \"View commit should have checkpoint\")\n\n\tt.Log(\"Committing controller.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add Name to Controller\", \"controller.go\")\n\tcheckpointController := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpointController, \"Controller commit should have checkpoint\")\n\n\t// All three checkpoints should be different\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpointModel, checkpointView)\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpointView, checkpointController)\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpointModel, checkpointController)\n\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoints: model=%s, view=%s, controller=%s\",\n\t\tcheckpointModel, checkpointView, checkpointController)\n\n\t// Validate each checkpoint has the correct files_touched\n\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\tCheckpointID: checkpointModel,\n\t\tStrategy:     \"manual-commit\",\n\t\tFilesTouched: []string{\"model.go\"},\n\t})\n\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\tCheckpointID: checkpointView,\n\t\tStrategy:     \"manual-commit\",\n\t\tFilesTouched: []string{\"view.go\"},\n\t})\n\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\tCheckpointID: checkpointController,\n\t\tStrategy:     \"manual-commit\",\n\t\tFilesTouched: []string{\"controller.go\"},\n\t})\n}\n\n// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification tests content-aware overlap detection\n// when user reverts agent's modification to an existing file and makes their own changes.\nfunc TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\n\tenv := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, \"manual-commit\")\n\n\t// Create and commit an existing file\n\toriginalContent := `package main\n\nfunc Calculate(x, y int) int {\n\treturn x + y\n}\n`\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"calc.go\", originalContent)\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add calculator\", \"calc.go\")\n\n\t// Agent modifies the file\n\tt.Log(\"Agent modifying calc.go\")\n\tprompt := `Modify calc.go to add a Multiply function that multiplies two integers.\nKeep the existing Calculate function. Only modify this file.`\n\n\tresult, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\t// Verify agent modified the file\n\tmodifiedContent := env.ReadFile(\"calc.go\")\n\tassert.Contains(t, modifiedContent, \"Multiply\", \"calc.go should have Multiply function\")\n\n\t// User reverts to original and writes completely different changes\n\tt.Log(\"User reverting and writing different changes\")\n\tuserContent := `package main\n\nfunc Calculate(x, y int) int {\n\treturn x + y\n}\n\nfunc Subtract(x, y int) int {\n\treturn x - y\n}\n`\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"calc.go\", userContent)\n\n\t// User commits their changes (not the agent's)\n\tt.Log(\"Committing user's changes\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add Subtract function\", \"calc.go\")\n\n\t// Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint trailer\n\t// because user's content doesn't match agent's content\n\tcheckpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint IDs: %v\", checkpointIDs)\n\n\t// The commit should NOT have a checkpoint trailer because the content\n\t// is completely different from what the agent wrote\n\tlatestCheckpoint := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\tassert.Empty(t, latestCheckpoint,\n\t\t\"Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint when user reverts agent's changes\")\n}\n\n// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified tests a scenario where the agent\n// both creates new files AND modifies existing files in the same session.\nfunc TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\n\tenv := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, \"manual-commit\")\n\n\t// Create and commit an existing file\n\tenv.WriteFile(\"main.go\", `package main\n\nfunc main() {\n\t// TODO: add imports\n}\n`)\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add main.go\", \"main.go\")\n\n\t// Agent modifies existing file AND creates new files\n\tt.Log(\"Agent modifying main.go and creating new files\")\n\tprompt := `Do these tasks:\n1. Create a new file utils.go with: package main; func Helper() string { return \"helper\" }\n2. Create a new file types.go with: package main; type Config struct { Name string }\n3. Modify main.go to add a comment \"// imports utils and types\" at the top (after package main)\nComplete all three tasks.`\n\n\tresult, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\t// Verify all changes\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"utils.go\"), \"utils.go should exist\")\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"types.go\"), \"types.go should exist\")\n\tmainContent := env.ReadFile(\"main.go\")\n\tassert.Contains(t, mainContent, \"imports utils and types\", \"main.go should be modified\")\n\n\t// User commits existing file modification first\n\tt.Log(\"Committing main.go modification\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Update main.go imports comment\", \"main.go\")\n\tcheckpoint1 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint1, \"main.go commit should have checkpoint\")\n\n\t// User commits new files together\n\tt.Log(\"Committing new files utils.go and types.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add utils and types\", \"utils.go\", \"types.go\")\n\tcheckpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()\n\trequire.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, \"New files commit should have checkpoint\")\n\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, \"Checkpoints should be different\")\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint 1 (modified): %s, Checkpoint 2 (new): %s\", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)\n}"
```json
}
```

All tests pass. Here's a summary of the new e2e tests I added for scenarios with existing files:

**New tests in `scenario_checkpoint_workflows_test.go`:**

1. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_ModifyAndCommit`**
   - Agent modifies an existing tracked file
   - User commits the modification
   - Verifies checkpoint is created

2. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications`**
   - Agent modifies two existing tracked files
   - User commits one, stashes the other
   - User pops stash and commits the second file
   - Verifies both get separate checkpoints
   - Tests that standard `git stash` (without `-u`) works for tracked file modifications

3. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits`**
   - Agent modifies three existing files (model.go, view.go, controller.go)
   - User commits each separately
   - Validates each checkpoint has correct `files_touched`
   - Similar to Scenario 4 but with modifications instead of new files

4. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification`**
   - Agent modifies existing file (adds Multiply function)
   - User reverts and writes different changes (adds Subtract function)
   - Verifies content-aware detection prevents checkpoint trailer
   - Tests Bug 3 fix with existing files

5. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified`**
   - Agent creates new files AND modifies existing file in same session
   - User commits modifications and new files separately
   - Verifies both commits get checkpoints

Also added `GetLatestCheckpointID()` helper that returns the checkpoint from HEAD commit (empty string if none) for test convenience.

Looking at the failures, there are two distinct issues:

```
    14→// Content-aware overlap detection for checkpoint management.
    15→//
    16→// These functions determine whether a commit contains session-related work by comparing
    17→// file content (not just filenames) against the shadow branch. This enables accurate
    18→// detection of the "reverted and replaced" scenario where a user:
    19→// 1. Reverts session changes (e.g., git checkout -- file.txt)
    20→// 2. Creates completely different content in the same file
    21→// 3. Commits the new content
    22→//
    23→// In this scenario, the commit should NOT get a checkpoint trailer because the
    24→// session's work was discarded, not incorporated.
    25→//
    26→// The key distinction:
    27→// - Modified files (exist in parent commit): Always count as overlap, regardless of
    28→//   content changes. The user is editing session's work.
    29→// - New files (don't exist in parent): Require content match against shadow branch.
    30→//   If content differs completely, the session's work was likely reverted & replaced.
    31→
```

> AGENT

**The Carry-Forward Scenario:**

1. Agent creates files A, B, C, D in one prompt
2. User commits only A and B → first checkpoint created
3. Files C and D are "carried forward" - they're still uncommitted but tracked in `state.FilesTouched`
4. User commits C and D → should get second checkpoint

**What was happening:**

After the first commit + condensation:
- The shadow branch gets updated/moved to point to the condensed checkpoint
- `state.FilesTouched` is updated to `[C, D]` (the remaining uncommitted files)
- But files C and D were **never written to the shadow branch tree** - they only existed in the working directory

When the second commit happens, `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent` does:
```go
// Check if file C is in the shadow branch tree
shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File("C")
if err != nil {
    // File not found in shadow tree
    continue  // ← OLD: Skip this file, check next one
}
```

Since C and D don't exist in the shadow branch tree, they were being skipped. If no files matched, the function returned `false` (no overlap), so no checkpoint was created.

**The fix:**

```go
shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(stagedPath)
if err != nil {
    // File is in filesTouched but NOT in shadow tree.
    // This is a carry-forward file: session tracked it, but shadow 
    // branch was moved after condensation. Trust filesTouched.
    return true  // ← NEW: Count as overlap
}
```

The key insight: if a file is in `state.FilesTouched`, the session DID touch it. Even if it's not in the shadow branch tree (because the branch was reset after condensation), we should trust `FilesTouched` and create a checkpoint for it.

> AGENT

You're right, let me clarify. I got the details wrong.

**What actually happens:**

1. Agent creates A, B, C, D
2. Agent stops → Shadow branch `entire/<hash1>-xxx` is created with A, B, C, D in its tree
3. User commits A, B → Condensation happens
4. `state.BaseCommit` is updated to the new commit hash (`<hash2>`)
5. Shadow branch name is derived from BaseCommit: `entire/<hash2>-xxx`
6. User commits C, D

**The problem:**

At step 6, when we look up the shadow branch:
```go
shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
// Returns "entire/<hash2>-xxx"
```

But `entire/<hash2>-xxx` **doesn't exist**! The files are still in the OLD shadow branch `entire/<hash1>-xxx`, but we're looking at a different branch name because `BaseCommit` changed.

So when `shadowTree.File("C")` fails, it's not because C was never written to any shadow branch - it's because we're looking at the wrong branch (the new one that doesn't exist, not the old one that has the files).

**The fix logic:**

Since the file IS in `state.FilesTouched` (the session tracked it), and it's a new file being staged, we trust that it's session-related even if we can't find it in the current shadow branch tree. The `FilesTouched` list is the source of truth for carry-forward files.

```
   333→}
   334→
   335→// filesWithRemainingAgentChanges returns files from filesTouched that still have
   336→// uncommitted agent changes. This is used for carry-forward after partial commits.
   337→//
   338→// A file has remaining agent changes if:
   339→//   - It wasn't committed at all (not in committedFiles), OR
   340→//   - It was committed but the committed content doesn't match the shadow branch
   341→//     (user committed partial changes, e.g., via git add -p)
   342→//
   343→// Falls back to file-level subtraction if shadow branch is unavailable.
   344→func filesWithRemainingAgentChanges(
   345→	repo *git.Repository,
   346→	shadowBranchName string,
   347→	headCommit *object.Commit,
   348→	filesTouched []string,
   349→	committedFiles map[string]struct{},
   350→) []string {
   351→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   352→
   353→	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
   354→	commitTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   355→	if err != nil {
   356→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get commit tree, falling back to file subtraction",
   357→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   358→		)
   359→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   360→	}
   361→
   362→	// Get shadow branch tree (the session's full content)
   363→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   364→	shadowRef, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   365→	if err != nil {
   366→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: shadow branch not found, falling back to file subtraction",
   367→			slog.String("branch", shadowBranchName),
   368→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   369→		)
   370→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   371→	}
   372→
   373→	shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
   374→	if err != nil {
   375→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get shadow commit, falling back to file subtraction",
   376→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   377→		)
   378→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   379→	}
   380→
   381→	shadowTree, err := shadowCommit.Tree()
   382→	if err != nil {
   383→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to file subtraction",
   384→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   385→		)
   386→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   387→	}
   388→
   389→	var remaining []string
   390→
   391→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
   392→		// If file wasn't committed at all, it definitely has remaining changes
   393→		if _, wasCommitted := committedFiles[filePath]; !wasCommitted {
   394→			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)
   395→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: file not committed, keeping",
   396→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   397→			)
   398→			continue
   399→		}
   400→
   401→		// File was committed - check if committed content matches shadow branch
   402→		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(filePath)
   403→		if err != nil {
   404→			// File not in shadow branch - nothing to carry forward for this file
   405→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: file not in shadow branch, skipping",
   406→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   407→			)
   408→			continue
   409→		}
   410→
   411→		commitFile, err := commitTree.File(filePath)
   412→		if err != nil {
   413→			// File not in commit tree (deleted?) - keep it if it's in shadow
   414→			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)
   415→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: file not in commit tree but in shadow, keeping",
   416→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   417→			)
   418→			continue
   419→		}
   420→
   421→		// Compare hashes - if different, there are still uncommitted agent changes
   422→		if commitFile.Hash != shadowFile.Hash {
   423→			remaining = append(remaining, filePath)
   424→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: content mismatch, keeping for carry-forward",
   425→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   426→				slog.String("commit_hash", commitFile.Hash.String()[:7]),
   427→				slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()[:7]),
   428→			)
   429→		} else {
   430→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: content fully committed",
   431→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   432→			)
   433→		}
   434→	}
   435→
   436→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: result",
   437→		slog.Int("files_touched", len(filesTouched)),
   438→		slog.Int("committed_files", len(committedFiles)),
   439→		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remaining)),
   440→	)
   441→
   442→	return remaining
```

I see the bug in my fix! In PostCommit, `getStagedFiles()` returns empty because files are already committed. So:

```go
if hasUncommittedFiles {
    stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
    if len(stagedFiles) > 0 {  // This is false in PostCommit!
        return stagedFilesOverlapWithContent(...), nil
    }
    // Falls through - no return here!
}

return hasTranscriptGrowth, nil  // Returns false!
```

```
    29→
    30→// hasTTY checks if /dev/tty is available for interactive prompts.
    31→// Returns false when running as an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
    32→//
    33→// In test environments, ENTIRE_TEST_TTY overrides the real check:
    34→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 → simulate human (TTY available)
    35→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 → simulate agent (no TTY)
    36→func hasTTY() bool {
    37→	if v := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"); v != "" {
    38→		return v == "1"
    39→	}
    40→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    41→	if err != nil {
    42→		return false
    43→	}
    44→	_ = tty.Close()
    45→	return true
    46→}
    47→
    48→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.
    49→// This works even when stdin is redirected (e.g., git commit -m).
    50→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    51→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    52→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    53→	// In test mode, don't try to interact with the real TTY — just use the default.
    54→	// ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 simulates "a human is present" for the hasTTY() check
    55→	// but we can't actually read from the TTY in tests.
    56→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY") != "" {
    57→		return defaultYes
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    61→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    62→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    63→	if err != nil {
    64→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    65→		return defaultYes
    66→	}
    67→	defer tty.Close()
    68→
    69→	// Show context if provided
    70→	if context != "" {
    71→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    72→	}
    73→
    74→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    75→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    76→	var hint string
    77→	if defaultYes {
    78→		hint = "[Y/n]"
    79→	} else {
    80→		hint = "[y/N]"
    81→	}
    82→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    83→
    84→	// Read response
    85→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    86→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
```

```
   843→	// Get shadow branch
   844→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   845→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   846→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   847→	if err != nil {

   849→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.

   852→	}

   857→	}
   858→
   859→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   860→	if err != nil {

   874→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   875→		hasTranscriptFile = true

   877→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, content)
   878→		}

   882→	// check if the session has FilesTouched. Carry-forward sets FilesTouched with remaining files.
   883→	if !hasTranscriptFile {
```

```
   151→func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) RunPromptWithTools(ctx context.Context, workDir string, prompt string, tools []string) (*AgentResult, error) {
   152→	// Build command: claude --model <model> -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools <tools>
   153→	args := []string{
   154→		"--model", r.Model,
   155→		"-p", prompt,
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	if len(tools) > 0 {
   159→		// Claude CLI expects each tool as a separate argument after --allowedTools
   160→		// e.g., --allowedTools Edit Read Bash (not --allowedTools "Edit,Read,Bash")
   161→		args = append(args, "--allowedTools")
   162→		args = append(args, tools...)
   163→	}

   165→	// Create context with timeout

   168→
   169→	//nolint:gosec // args are constructed from trusted config, not user input
   170→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", args...)
   171→	cmd.Dir = workDir

   174→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   175→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   176→
   177→	start := time.Now()
   178→	err := cmd.Run()
   179→	duration := time.Since(start)
   180→
   181→	result := &AgentResult{
   182→		Stdout:   stdout.String(),
   183→		Stderr:   stderr.String(),
   184→		Duration: duration,
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	if err != nil {

   191→		} else {
   192→			result.ExitCode = -1
   193→		}
   194→		//nolint:wrapcheck // error is from exec.Run, caller can check ExitCode in result
   195→		return result, err
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	result.ExitCode = 0
   199→	return result, nil
   200→}
```

```
   106→// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.
   107→// checkpointID is the 12-hex-char value from the Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   108→// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/

   110→//
   111→// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveChanges called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.
   112→// In this case, data is extracted from the live transcript instead.
   113→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState, committedFiles map[string]struct{}) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   114→	// Get shadow branch (may not exist for mid-session commits)

   126→		// potentially stale shadow branch copy (SaveChanges may have been skipped if the
   127→		// last turn had no code changes).

   130→		if err != nil {

   135→		// Extract data directly from live transcript.
   136→		if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
   137→			return nil, errors.New("shadow branch not found and no live transcript available")
```

> AGENT

Let me trace through how `TestE2E_Scenario4_UserSplitsCommits` works with the current implementation:

## Scenario 4: Single Session Split Commits

### Setup
1. User runs a single prompt that creates files A, B, C, D
2. User commits A, B first
3. User commits C, D later
4. Both commits should get separate checkpoint IDs

### Detailed Flow

**Step 1: Agent creates files A, B, C, D**
```
- user-prompt-submit hook → session starts (ACTIVE)
- Agent creates fileA.go, fileB.go, fileC.go, fileD.go
- stop hook → SaveChanges called:
  - Creates shadow branch `entire/<HEAD>-<worktreeID>`
  - Shadow branch contains: A, B, C, D files + `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/full.jsonl`
  - State: StepCount=1, FilesTouched=[A,B,C,D], CheckpointTranscriptStart=0
- Session transitions to IDLE
```

**Step 2: User commits A, B only**
```
PrepareCommitMsg:
- Session is IDLE with StepCount=1, FilesTouched=[A,B,C,D]
- sessionHasNewContent() is called:
  - Shadow branch exists with transcript
  - hasTranscriptGrowth = (transcriptLines > 0) = true
  - stagedFiles = [A, B]
  - stagedFilesOverlapWithContent() checks [A,B] vs [A,B,C,D] → overlap found → true
- Checkpoint trailer added to commit message

PostCommit:
- filesOverlapWithContent() verifies A, B match shadow branch content → true
- CondenseSession() runs:
  - Writes checkpoint to entire/checkpoints/v1 with files_touched=[A,B]
  - Returns TotalTranscriptLines
- condenseAndUpdateState():
  - BaseCommit updated to new HEAD
  - StepCount = 0
  - CheckpointTranscriptStart = TotalTranscriptLines
  - FilesTouched = nil  ← CLEARED!
- carryForwardToNewShadowBranch():
  - Computes remaining files: [C, D] (files in shadow tree but not in commit)
  - Creates NEW shadow branch `entire/<new-HEAD>-<worktreeID>` with C, D only (NO metadata)
  - Updates state: FilesTouched=[C,D], StepCount=1, CheckpointTranscriptStart=0
- Old shadow branch deleted
```

**Step 3: User commits C, D**
```
PrepareCommitMsg:
- Session is IDLE with StepCount=1, FilesTouched=[C,D]
- sessionHasNewContent() is called:
  - Shadow branch exists (from carry-forward)
  - Looking for transcript at `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/full.jsonl`
  - NOT FOUND! (carry-forward doesn't include metadata)
  - hasTranscriptFile = false
  - len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 = true ([C,D])
  - stagedFiles = [C, D]
  - MY FIX: stagedFilesOverlapWithContent() checks [C,D] vs [C,D] → overlap → true
- Checkpoint trailer added

PostCommit:
- filesOverlapWithContent() verifies C, D match shadow branch content → true
- CondenseSession() runs:
  - Extracts transcript from LIVE transcript file (state.TranscriptPath)
  - Writes checkpoint to entire/checkpoints/v1 with files_touched=[C,D]
- Shadow branch deleted
- Session state cleared
```

### The Key Fix

The fix I made is in `sessionHasNewContent()` for the case when `!hasTranscriptFile`:

```go
if !hasTranscriptFile {
    if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 {
        stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
        if len(stagedFiles) > 0 {
            // PrepareCommitMsg: check staged files overlap
            return stagedFilesOverlapWithContent(repo, tree, stagedFiles, state.FilesTouched), nil
        }
        // PostCommit: return true, let caller do overlap check
        return true, nil
    }
    return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
}
```

**Before my fix:** When the shadow branch had no transcript (carry-forward case), it would call `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent()` without checking if `stagedFiles` was empty. In PostCommit, `stagedFiles` is empty (files already committed), so it would return `false`.

**After my fix:** If `stagedFiles` is empty but `FilesTouched` is not empty, we return `true` and let the caller (PostCommit) do its own overlap check using `filesOverlapWithContent()` with the committed files.

```

- State 1: BaseCommit=commit-A, FilesTouched=[B,C], StepCount=1, CheckpointTranscriptStart=0
```

```
    56→func (s *GitStore) WriteTemporary(ctx context.Context, opts WriteTemporaryOptions) (WriteTemporaryResult, error) {
    57→	// Validate base commit - required for shadow branch naming
    58→	if opts.BaseCommit == "" {
    59→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, errors.New("BaseCommit is required for temporary checkpoint")
    60→	}
    61→
    62→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    63→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
    64→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid temporary checkpoint options: %w", err)
    65→	}
    66→
    67→	// Get shadow branch name
    68→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(opts.BaseCommit, opts.WorktreeID)
    69→
    70→	// Get or create shadow branch
    71→	parentHash, baseTreeHash, err := s.getOrCreateShadowBranch(shadowBranchName)
    72→	if err != nil {
    73→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get shadow branch: %w", err)
    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Get the last checkpoint's tree hash for deduplication
    77→	var lastTreeHash plumbing.Hash
    78→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
    79→		if lastCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(parentHash); err == nil {
    80→			lastTreeHash = lastCommit.TreeHash
    81→		}
    82→	}
    83→
    84→	// Collect all files to include
    85→	var allFiles []string
    86→	var allDeletedFiles []string
    87→	if opts.IsFirstCheckpoint {
    88→		// For the first checkpoint, capture all changed files (modified tracked + untracked)
    89→		// using `git status --porcelain -z` which respects both repo and global .gitignore.
    90→		// This is much faster than filesystem walk. The base tree from HEAD already contains
    91→		// all unchanged tracked files. We also capture user's pre-existing deletions.
    92→		result, err := collectChangedFiles(ctx, s.repo)
    93→		if err != nil {
    94→			return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to collect changed files: %w", err)
    95→		}
    96→		allFiles = result.Changed
    97→		// Merge user's pre-existing deletions with agent's deletions
    98→		allDeletedFiles = result.Deleted
    99→		allDeletedFiles = append(allDeletedFiles, opts.DeletedFiles...)
   100→	} else {
   101→		// For subsequent checkpoints, only include modified/new files
   102→		allFiles = make([]string, 0, len(opts.ModifiedFiles)+len(opts.NewFiles))
   103→		allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.ModifiedFiles...)
   104→		allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.NewFiles...)
   105→		allDeletedFiles = opts.DeletedFiles
   106→	}
   107→
   108→	// Build tree with changes
   109→	treeHash, err := s.buildTreeWithChanges(baseTreeHash, allFiles, allDeletedFiles, opts.MetadataDir, opts.MetadataDirAbs)
   110→	if err != nil {
   111→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to build tree: %w", err)
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	// Deduplication: skip if tree hash matches the last checkpoint
   115→	if lastTreeHash != plumbing.ZeroHash && treeHash == lastTreeHash {
   116→		return WriteTemporaryResult{
   117→			CommitHash: parentHash,
   118→			Skipped:    true,
   119→		}, nil
   120→	}
   121→
   122→	// Create checkpoint commit with trailers
   123→	commitMsg := trailers.FormatShadowCommit(opts.CommitMessage, opts.MetadataDir, opts.SessionID)
   124→
   125→	commitHash, err := s.createCommit(treeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
   126→	if err != nil {
   127→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to create commit: %w", err)
   128→	}

   132→	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)

   134→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to update branch reference: %w", err)
   135→	}
   136→
   137→	return WriteTemporaryResult{
   138→		CommitHash: commitHash,
   139→		Skipped:    false,
   140→	}, nil
   141→}
```

```
  1807→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
  1808→	logCtx context.Context,
  1809→	repo *git.Repository,
  1810→	state *SessionState,
  1811→	remainingFiles []string,
  1812→) {
  1813→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1814→
  1815→	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
  1816→	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
  1817→	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
  1818→	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
  1819→	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
  1820→		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
  1821→		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
  1822→		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
  1823→		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
  1824→		MetadataDir:       "",
  1825→		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
  1826→		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
  1827→		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
  1828→	})
  1829→	if err != nil {
  1830→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
  1831→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1832→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1833→		)
  1834→		return
  1835→	}
  1836→	if result.Skipped {
  1837→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
  1838→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1839→		)
  1840→		return
  1841→	}
  1842→
  1843→	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
  1844→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
  1845→	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
  1846→	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
  1847→	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
  1848→	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
  1849→	//   the full transcript, which could be large
  1850→	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
  1851→	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.
  1852→	state.FilesTouched = remainingFiles
  1853→	state.StepCount = 1
  1854→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
  1855→	state.LastCheckpointID = ""

  1859→
  1860→	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: carried forward remaining files",
```

```
   151→func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) RunPromptWithTools(ctx context.Context, workDir string, prompt string, tools []string) (*AgentResult, error) {
   152→	// Build command: claude --model <model> -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools <tools>
   153→	args := []string{
   154→		"--model", r.Model,
   155→		"-p", prompt,
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	if len(tools) > 0 {
   159→		// Claude CLI expects each tool as a separate argument after --allowedTools
   160→		// e.g., --allowedTools Edit Read Bash (not --allowedTools "Edit,Read,Bash")
   161→		args = append(args, "--allowedTools")
   162→		args = append(args, tools...)
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Create context with timeout
   166→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.Timeout)
   167→	defer cancel()
   168→
   169→	//nolint:gosec // args are constructed from trusted config, not user input
   170→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", args...)
   171→	cmd.Dir = workDir
   172→
   173→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   174→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   175→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   176→
   177→	start := time.Now()
   178→	err := cmd.Run()
   179→	duration := time.Since(start)
   180→
   181→	result := &AgentResult{
   182→		Stdout:   stdout.String(),
   183→		Stderr:   stderr.String(),
   184→		Duration: duration,
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	if err != nil {
   188→		exitErr := &exec.ExitError{}
   189→		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   190→			result.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
   191→		} else {
   192→			result.ExitCode = -1
   193→		}
   194→		//nolint:wrapcheck // error is from exec.Run, caller can check ExitCode in result
   195→		return result, err
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	result.ExitCode = 0
   199→	return result, nil
   200→}
```

```
    52→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    53→	// In test mode, don't try to interact with the real TTY — just use the default.
    54→	// ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 simulates "a human is present" for the hasTTY() check
    55→	// but we can't actually read from the TTY in tests.
    56→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY") != "" {
    57→		return defaultYes
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    61→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    62→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    63→	if err != nil {
    64→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    65→		return defaultYes
    66→	}
    67→	defer tty.Close()
    68→
    69→	// Show context if provided
    70→	if context != "" {
    71→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    72→	}
    73→
    74→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    75→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    76→	var hint string
    77→	if defaultYes {
    78→		hint = "[Y/n]"
    79→	} else {
    80→		hint = "[y/N]"
    81→	}
    82→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    83→
    84→	// Read response
    85→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    86→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
    87→	if err != nil {
    88→		return defaultYes
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
    92→	switch response {
    93→	case "y", "yes":
    94→		return true
    95→	case "n", "no":
    96→		return false
    97→	default:
    98→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
    99→		return defaultYes
   100→	}
   101→}
```

```
    11→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
    12→type Phase string
    13→
    14→const (
    15→	PhaseActive Phase = "active"
    16→	PhaseIdle   Phase = "idle"
    17→	PhaseEnded  Phase = "ended"
    18→)
    19→
    20→// allPhases is the canonical list of phases for enumeration (e.g., diagram generation).
    21→var allPhases = []Phase{PhaseIdle, PhaseActive, PhaseEnded}
    22→
    23→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty or unknown values
    24→// as PhaseIdle for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
    25→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
    26→	switch Phase(s) {
    27→	case PhaseActive, "active_committed":
    28→		// "active_committed" was removed with the 1:1 checkpoint model.
    29→		// It previously meant "agent active + commit happened during turn".
    30→		// Normalize to ACTIVE so HandleTurnEnd can finalize any pending checkpoints.
    31→		return PhaseActive
    32→	case PhaseIdle:
    33→		return PhaseIdle
    34→	case PhaseEnded:
    35→		return PhaseEnded
    36→	default:
    37→		// Backward compat: truly unknown phases normalize to idle.
    38→		return PhaseIdle
    39→	}
    40→}
    41→
    42→// IsActive reports whether the phase represents an active agent turn.
    43→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
    44→	return p == PhaseActive
    45→}
    46→
    47→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
    48→type Event int
```

```
   690→func (s *GitStore) buildTreeWithChanges(
   691→	baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash,
   692→	modifiedFiles, deletedFiles []string,
   693→	metadataDir, metadataDirAbs string,
   694→) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   695→	// Get repo root for resolving file paths
   696→	// This is critical because fileExists() and createBlobFromFile() use os.Stat()
   697→	// which resolves relative to CWD. The modifiedFiles are repo-relative paths,
   698→	// so we must resolve them against repo root, not CWD.
   699→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   700→	if err != nil {
   701→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   702→	}
   703→
   704→	// Get the base tree
   705→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   706→	if err != nil {
   707→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   708→	}
   709→
   710→	// Flatten existing tree
   711→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   712→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   713→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten base tree: %w", err)
   714→	}
   715→
   716→	// Remove deleted files
   717→	for _, file := range deletedFiles {
   718→		delete(entries, file)
   719→	}
   720→
   721→	// Add/update modified files
   722→	for _, file := range modifiedFiles {
   723→		// Resolve path relative to repo root for filesystem operations
   724→		absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   725→		if !fileExists(absPath) {
   726→			delete(entries, file)
   727→			continue
   728→		}
   729→
   730→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(s.repo, absPath)
   731→		if err != nil {
   732→			// Skip files that can't be staged (may have been deleted since detection)
   733→			continue
   734→		}
   735→
   736→		entries[file] = object.TreeEntry{
   737→			Name: file,
   738→			Mode: mode,
   739→			Hash: blobHash,
   740→		}
   741→	}
   742→
   743→	// Add metadata directory files
   744→	if metadataDir != "" && metadataDirAbs != "" {
   745→		if err := addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(s.repo, metadataDirAbs, metadataDir, entries); err != nil {
   746→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to add metadata directory: %w", err)
   747→		}
   748→	}
   749→
   750→	// Build tree
   751→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   752→}

   755→func (s *GitStore) createCommit(treeHash, parentHash plumbing.Hash, message, authorName, authorEmail string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   756→	now := time.Now()
   757→	sig := object.Signature{
   758→		Name:  authorName,
   759→		Email: authorEmail,
   760→		When:  now,
   761→	}
   762→
   763→	commit := &object.Commit{
   764→		TreeHash:  treeHash,
   765→		Author:    sig,
   766→		Committer: sig,
   767→		Message:   message,
   768→	}
   769→
   770→	// Add parent if not a new branch
   771→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
   772→		commit.ParentHashes = []plumbing.Hash{parentHash}
   773→	}
   774→
   775→	obj := s.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   776→	if err := commit.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   777→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode commit: %w", err)
   778→	}
   779→
   780→	hash, err := s.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   781→	if err != nil {
   782→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store commit: %w", err)
   783→	}
   784→
   785→	return hash, nil
   786→}
```

```
   176→// SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID returns the path to a session's metadata directory
   177→// for the given Entire session ID. The sessionID must be the full, already date-prefixed
   178→// Entire session identifier as stored on disk, not an agent-specific or raw Claude ID.
   179→func SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID string) string {
   180→	return EntireMetadataDir + "/" + sessionID
   181→}
   182→
   183→// ExtractSessionIDFromTranscriptPath attempts to extract a session ID from a transcript path.
   184→// Claude transcripts are stored at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/sessions/<id>.jsonl
   185→// If the path doesn't match expected format, returns empty string.
   186→func ExtractSessionIDFromTranscriptPath(transcriptPath string) string {
   187→	// Try to extract from typical path: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/sessions/<id>.jsonl
   188→	parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(transcriptPath), "/")
   189→	for i, part := range parts {
   190→		if part == "sessions" && i+1 < len(parts) {
   191→			// Return filename without extension
   192→			filename := parts[i+1]
   193→			if strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".jsonl") {
   194→				return strings.TrimSuffix(filename, ".jsonl")
   195→			}
   196→			return filename
   197→		}
   198→	}
   199→	return ""
   200→}
```

```
   240→// handleSessionStartCommon is the shared implementation for session start hooks.
   241→// Used by both Claude Code and Gemini CLI handlers.
   242→func handleSessionStartCommon() error {
   243→	ag, err := GetCurrentHookAgent()
   244→	if err != nil {
   245→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   246→	}
   247→
   248→	input, err := ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookSessionStart, os.Stdin)
   249→	if err != nil {
   250→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook input: %w", err)
   251→	}
   252→
   253→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"), ag.Name())
   254→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session-start",
   255→		slog.String("hook", "session-start"),
   256→		slog.String("hook_type", "agent"),
   257→		slog.String("model_session_id", input.SessionID),
   258→		slog.String("transcript_path", input.SessionRef),
   259→	)
   260→
   261→	if input.SessionID == "" {
   262→		return errors.New("no session_id in input")
   263→	}
   264→
   265→	// Build informational message
   266→	message := "\n\nPowered by Entire:\n  This conversation will be linked to your next commit."
   267→
   268→	// Check for concurrent sessions and append count if any
   269→	strat := GetStrategy()
   270→	if concurrentChecker, ok := strat.(strategy.ConcurrentSessionChecker); ok {
   271→		if count, err := concurrentChecker.CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(input.SessionID); err == nil && count > 0 {
   272→			message += fmt.Sprintf("\n  %d other active conversation(s) in this workspace will also be included.\n  Use 'entire status' for more information.", count)
   273→		}
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Output informational message using agent-specific format
   277→	if err := outputHookResponse(message); err != nil {
   278→		return err
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	// Fire EventSessionStart for the current session (if state exists).
   282→	// This handles ENDED → IDLE (re-entering a session).
   283→	// TODO(ENT-221): dispatch ActionWarnStaleSession for ACTIVE sessions.
   284→	if state, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(input.SessionID); loadErr != nil {
   285→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state on start: %v\n", loadErr)
   286→	} else if state != nil {
   287→		strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventSessionStart, session.TransitionContext{})
   288→		if saveErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(state); saveErr != nil {
   289→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update session state on start: %v\n", saveErr)
   290→		}
   291→	}
   292→
   293→	return nil
   294→}
```

I found the issue! Looking at the debug output:

1. **Only ONE session state file exists** after both prompts
2. The session has `Phase=ended` and `FilesTouched=[stash_b.go stash_c.go]` (carry-forward from session 1)
3. **Session 2 was never created!**

This means when prompt 2 runs, either:
1. Claude CLI is reusing the same session ID
2. The hooks aren't creating a new session state

The shadow branch also shows no session 2 content - it only has the files from session 1's carry-forward.

Let me add more debug output to understand if the hooks are even being called for prompt 2.

> AGENT

Now I understand the issue. Claude CLI is reusing the same session ID for both prompts, and after prompt 1 the session phase is "ended". When prompt 2 runs, Claude CLI might be skipping hooks for an already-ended session.

The fact that the phase stays "ended" after prompt 2 (rather than transitioning to ACTIVE) confirms that **the hooks are not being invoked for prompt 2**.

This seems to be a Claude CLI behavior - it doesn't reinvoke hooks for a session that's already in the "ended" state. 

Let me check if there's a way to clear the ended session before running prompt 2, or if we need a different test approach. Let me look at how to delete the session state file between prompts.

```
   211→
   212→	_, err = worktree.Commit(message, &git.CommitOptions{
   213→		Author: &object.Signature{
   214→			Name:  "E2E Test User",
   215→			Email: "e2e-test@example.com",
   216→			When:  time.Now(),

   224→// GitCommitWithShadowHooks stages and commits files, running the prepare-commit-msg
   225→// and post-commit hooks like a real workflow.
   226→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   227→	env.T.Helper()
   228→
   229→	// Stage files using go-git
   230→	for _, file := range files {
   231→		env.GitAdd(file)
   232→	}
   233→
   234→	// Create a temp file for the commit message
   235→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
   236→	//nolint:gosec // test code, permissions are intentionally standard
   237→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
   238→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook
   242→	//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code, args are from trusted test setup, no context needed
   243→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "message")
   244→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   245→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   246→		"ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1",
   247→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".claude"),
   248→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".gemini"),
   249→	)
   250→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   251→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
   252→	}
   253→
   254→	// Read the modified message
   255→	//nolint:gosec // test code, path is from test setup
   256→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
   257→	if err != nil {
   258→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
   259→	}
   260→
   261→	// Create the commit using go-git with the modified message
   262→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   263→	if err != nil {
   264→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   265→	}
   266→
   267→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   268→	if err != nil {
   269→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
   270→	}
   271→
   272→	_, err = worktree.Commit(string(modifiedMsg), &git.CommitOptions{
   273→		Author: &object.Signature{
   274→			Name:  "E2E Test User",
   275→			Email: "e2e-test@example.com",
   276→			When:  time.Now(),
   277→		},
   278→	})
   279→	if err != nil {
   280→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
   281→	}
   282→
   283→	// Run post-commit hook
   284→	//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code, args are from trusted test setup, no context needed
   285→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
   286→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   287→	postCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   288→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".claude"),
   289→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".gemini"),
   290→	)
   291→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   292→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
   293→	}
   294→}

   326→type RewindPoint struct {
   327→	ID               string    `json:"id"`
   328→	Message          string    `json:"message"`
   329→	MetadataDir      string    `json:"metadata_dir"`
   330→	Date             time.Time `json:"date"`
   331→	IsTaskCheckpoint bool      `json:"is_task_checkpoint"`
   332→	ToolUseID        string    `json:"tool_use_id"`
   333→	IsLogsOnly       bool      `json:"is_logs_only"`

   337→// GetRewindPoints returns available rewind points using the CLI.
   338→func (env *TestEnv) GetRewindPoints() []RewindPoint {
   339→	env.T.Helper()
   340→
   341→	//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code, args are static, no context needed
   342→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "rewind", "--list")
   343→	cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   344→
   345→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   346→	if err != nil {
   347→		env.T.Fatalf("rewind --list failed: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   348→	}
   349→
   350→	// Parse JSON output
   351→	var jsonPoints []struct {
   352→		ID               string `json:"id"`
   353→		Message          string `json:"message"`
   354→		MetadataDir      string `json:"metadata_dir"`
   355→		Date             string `json:"date"`
   356→		IsTaskCheckpoint bool   `json:"is_task_checkpoint"`
   357→		ToolUseID        string `json:"tool_use_id"`
   358→		IsLogsOnly       bool   `json:"is_logs_only"`
   359→		CondensationID   string `json:"condensation_id"`
   360→	}
   361→
   362→	if err := json.Unmarshal(output, &jsonPoints); err != nil {
   363→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to parse rewind points: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   364→	}
   365→
   366→	points := make([]RewindPoint, len(jsonPoints))
   367→	for i, jp := range jsonPoints {
   368→		//nolint:errcheck // date parsing failure is acceptable, defaults to zero time
   369→		date, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, jp.Date)
   370→		points[i] = RewindPoint{
   371→			ID:               jp.ID,
   372→			Message:          jp.Message,
   373→			MetadataDir:      jp.MetadataDir,
   374→			Date:             date,
   375→			IsTaskCheckpoint: jp.IsTaskCheckpoint,
   376→			ToolUseID:        jp.ToolUseID,
   377→			IsLogsOnly:       jp.IsLogsOnly,
   378→			CondensationID:   jp.CondensationID,
   379→		}
   380→	}
   381→
   382→	return points
   383→}

   446→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD and returns
   447→// the checkpoint ID from the first commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   448→// Returns an error if no checkpoint trailer is found in any commit.
   449→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() (string, error) {
   450→	env.T.Helper()
   451→
   452→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   453→	if err != nil {
   454→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   455→	}
   456→
   457→	head, err := repo.Head()
   458→	if err != nil {
   459→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
   460→	}
   461→
   462→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
   463→	if err != nil {
   464→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
   465→	}
   466→
   467→	var checkpointID string
   468→	//nolint:errcheck,gosec // ForEach callback returns error to stop iteration, not a real error
   469→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   470→		// Look for Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   471→		for _, line := range strings.Split(c.Message, "\n") {
   472→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   473→			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
   474→				checkpointID = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:"))
   475→				return errors.New("stop iteration")
   476→			}
   477→		}
   478→		return nil
   479→	})
   480→
   481→	if checkpointID == "" {
   482→		return "", errors.New("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
   483→	}
   484→
   485→	return checkpointID, nil
   486→}
   487→
   488→// GetLatestCheckpointID returns the checkpoint ID from HEAD commit, or empty string if none.
   489→// This is a convenience wrapper that doesn't fail the test on missing checkpoint.
   490→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointID() string {
   491→	env.T.Helper()
   492→
   493→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   494→	if err != nil {
   495→		return ""
   496→	}
   497→
   498→	head, err := repo.Head()
   499→	if err != nil {
   500→		return ""
   501→	}
   502→
   503→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   504→	if err != nil {
   505→		return ""
   506→	}
   507→
   508→	// Look for Entire-Checkpoint trailer in HEAD commit only
   509→	for _, line := range strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n") {
   510→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   511→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
   512→			return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:"))
   513→		}
   514→	}
   515→	return ""
   516→}

   518→// safeIDPrefix returns first 12 chars of ID or the full ID if shorter.
   519→// Use this when logging checkpoint IDs to avoid index out of bounds panic.
   520→func safeIDPrefix(id string) string {
   521→	if len(id) >= 12 {
   522→		return id[:12]
   523→	}
   524→	return id

   675→// ReadFileFromBranch reads a file's content from a specific branch's tree.
   676→// Returns the content and true if found, empty string and false if not found.
   677→func (env *TestEnv) ReadFileFromBranch(branchName, filePath string) (string, bool) {
   678→	env.T.Helper()
   679→
   680→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   681→	if err != nil {
   682→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   683→	}
   684→
   685→	// Get the branch reference
   686→	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), true)
   687→	if err != nil {
   688→		// Try as a remote-style ref
   689→		ref, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/"+branchName), true)
   690→		if err != nil {
   691→			return "", false
   692→		}
   693→	}
   694→
   695→	// Get the commit
   696→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   697→	if err != nil {
   698→		return "", false
   699→	}
   700→
   701→	// Get the tree
   702→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   703→	if err != nil {
   704→		return "", false
   705→	}
   706→
   707→	// Get the file
   708→	file, err := tree.File(filePath)
   709→	if err != nil {
   710→		return "", false
   711→	}
   712→
   713→	// Get the content
   714→	content, err := file.Contents()
   715→	if err != nil {
   716→		return "", false
   717→	}
   718→
   719→	return content, true
   720→}

   722→// CheckpointValidation contains expected values for checkpoint validation.
   723→type CheckpointValidation struct {
   724→	// CheckpointID is the expected checkpoint ID
   725→	CheckpointID string
   726→
   727→	// Strategy is the expected strategy name (optional)
   728→	Strategy string
   729→
   730→	// FilesTouched are the expected files in files_touched (optional)
   731→	FilesTouched []string
   732→
   733→	// ExpectedPrompts are strings that should appear in prompt.txt (optional)

   739→
   740→// ValidateCheckpoint performs comprehensive validation of a checkpoint on the metadata branch.
   741→func (env *TestEnv) ValidateCheckpoint(v CheckpointValidation) {
   742→	env.T.Helper()
   743→
   744→	metadataBranch := "entire/checkpoints/v1"
   745→
   746→	// Compute sharded path: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
   747→	if len(v.CheckpointID) < 3 {
   748→		env.T.Fatalf("Checkpoint ID too short: %s", v.CheckpointID)
   749→	}
   750→	shardedPath := v.CheckpointID[:2] + "/" + v.CheckpointID[2:]
   751→
   752→	// Validate root metadata.json exists and has expected fields
   753→	summaryPath := shardedPath + "/metadata.json"
   754→	summaryContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, summaryPath)
   755→	if !found {
   756→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary not found at %s", summaryPath)
   757→	} else {
   758→		var summary map[string]any
   759→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(summaryContent), &summary); err != nil {
   760→			env.T.Errorf("Failed to parse CheckpointSummary: %v", err)
   761→		} else {
   762→			// Validate checkpoint_id
   763→			if cpID, ok := summary["checkpoint_id"].(string); !ok || cpID != v.CheckpointID {
   764→				env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.checkpoint_id = %v, want %s", summary["checkpoint_id"], v.CheckpointID)
   765→			}
   766→			// Validate strategy if specified
   767→			if v.Strategy != "" {

   771→			}
   772→			// Validate sessions array exists
   773→			if sessions, ok := summary["sessions"].([]any); !ok || len(sessions) == 0 {
   774→				env.T.Error("CheckpointSummary.sessions should have at least one entry")
   775→			}
   776→			// Validate files_touched if specified
   777→			if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   778→				if filesTouched, ok := summary["files_touched"].([]any); ok {
   779→					touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
   780→					for _, f := range filesTouched {
   781→						if s, ok := f.(string); ok {
   782→							touchedSet[s] = true
   783→						}
   784→					}
   785→					for _, expected := range v.FilesTouched {
   786→						if !touchedSet[expected] {
   787→							env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.files_touched missing %q", expected)
   788→						}
   789→					}
   790→				}
   791→			}
   792→		}
   793→	}

   795→	// Validate session metadata.json exists
   796→	sessionMetadataPath := shardedPath + "/0/metadata.json"
   797→	sessionContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, sessionMetadataPath)
   798→	if !found {
   799→		env.T.Errorf("Session metadata not found at %s", sessionMetadataPath)
   800→	} else {
   801→		var metadata map[string]any
   802→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionContent), &metadata); err != nil {
   803→			env.T.Errorf("Failed to parse session metadata: %v", err)
   804→		} else {
   805→			// Validate checkpoint_id matches
   806→			if cpID, ok := metadata["checkpoint_id"].(string); !ok || cpID != v.CheckpointID {

   808→			}

   811→				env.T.Error("Session metadata.created_at should exist")
   812→			}
   813→		}
   814→	}
   815→
   816→	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
   817→	transcriptPath := shardedPath + "/0/full.jsonl"
   818→	transcriptContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, transcriptPath)
   819→	if !found {
   820→		env.T.Errorf("Transcript not found at %s", transcriptPath)
   821→	} else {
   822→		// Check each line is valid JSON
   823→		lines := strings.Split(transcriptContent, "\n")
   824→		validLines := 0
   825→		for i, line := range lines {
   826→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   827→			if line == "" {
   828→				continue
   829→			}
   830→			validLines++
   831→			var obj map[string]any
   832→			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
   833→				env.T.Errorf("Transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v", i+1, err)
   834→			}
   835→		}
   836→		if validLines == 0 {
   837→			env.T.Error("Transcript is empty (no valid JSONL lines)")
   838→		}

   840→		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedTranscriptContent {
   841→			if !strings.Contains(transcriptContent, expected) {

   843→			}
   844→		}
   845→	}
   846→

   851→		if !found {

   853→		} else {
   854→			for _, expected := range v.ExpectedPrompts {

   856→					env.T.Errorf("Prompt file should contain %q", expected)
   857→				}
   858→			}
   859→		}
   860→	}
   861→
   862→	// Validate content hash exists and matches transcript
   863→	hashPath := shardedPath + "/0/content_hash.txt"
   864→	hashContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, hashPath)
   865→	if !found {
   866→		env.T.Errorf("Content hash not found at %s", hashPath)
   867→	} else if transcriptContent != "" {
   868→		// Verify hash matches
   869→		hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcriptContent))

   871→		storedHash := strings.TrimSpace(hashContent)
   872→		if storedHash != expectedHash {
   873→			env.T.Errorf("Content hash mismatch:\n  stored:   %s\n  expected: %s", storedHash, expectedHash)
   874→		}
   875→	}
```

```
   129→func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) IsAvailable() (bool, error) {

   151→func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) RunPromptWithTools(ctx context.Context, workDir string, prompt string, tools []string) (*AgentResult, error) {
   152→	// Build command: claude --model <model> -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools <tools>
   153→	args := []string{
   154→		"--model", r.Model,
   155→		"-p", prompt,
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	if len(tools) > 0 {
   159→		// Claude CLI expects each tool as a separate argument after --allowedTools
   160→		// e.g., --allowedTools Edit Read Bash (not --allowedTools "Edit,Read,Bash")
   161→		args = append(args, "--allowedTools")
   162→		args = append(args, tools...)
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Create context with timeout
   166→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.Timeout)
   167→	defer cancel()
   168→
   169→	//nolint:gosec // args are constructed from trusted config, not user input
   170→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", args...)
   171→	cmd.Dir = workDir
   172→
   173→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   174→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   175→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   176→
   177→	start := time.Now()
   178→	err := cmd.Run()
   179→	duration := time.Since(start)
   180→
   181→	result := &AgentResult{
   182→		Stdout:   stdout.String(),
   183→		Stderr:   stderr.String(),
   184→		Duration: duration,
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	if err != nil {
   188→		exitErr := &exec.ExitError{}
   189→		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   190→			result.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
   191→		} else {
   192→			result.ExitCode = -1
   193→		}
   194→		//nolint:wrapcheck // error is from exec.Run, caller can check ExitCode in result
   195→		return result, err
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	result.ExitCode = 0
   199→	return result, nil
   200→}
```

```
   133→	if localDev {

   186→	if denyRaw, ok := rawPermissions["deny"]; ok {

   244→// parseHookType parses a specific hook type from rawHooks into the target slice.
   245→// Silently ignores parse errors (leaves target unchanged).
   246→func parseHookType(rawHooks map[string]json.RawMessage, hookType string, target *[]ClaudeHookMatcher) {
   247→	if data, ok := rawHooks[hookType]; ok {
   248→		//nolint:errcheck,gosec // Intentionally ignoring parse errors - leave target as nil/empty
   249→		json.Unmarshal(data, target)
   250→	}
   251→}
   252→
   253→// marshalHookType marshals a hook type back to rawHooks.
   254→// If the slice is empty, removes the key from rawHooks.
   255→func marshalHookType(rawHooks map[string]json.RawMessage, hookType string, matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher) {
   256→	if len(matchers) == 0 {
   257→		delete(rawHooks, hookType)
   258→		return
   259→	}
   260→	data, err := json.Marshal(matchers)
   261→	if err != nil {
   262→		return // Silently ignore marshal errors (shouldn't happen)
   263→	}
   264→	rawHooks[hookType] = data
   265→}

   267→// UninstallHooks removes Entire hooks from Claude Code settings.
   268→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) UninstallHooks() error {
   269→	// Use repo root to find .claude directory when run from a subdirectory
   270→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   271→	if err != nil {
   272→		repoRoot = "." // Fallback to CWD if not in a git repo
   273→	}
   274→	settingsPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".claude", ClaudeSettingsFileName)
   275→	data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath) //nolint:gosec // path is constructed from repo root + fixed path
   276→	if err != nil {
   277→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // No settings file means nothing to uninstall
   278→	}
   279→
   280→	var rawSettings map[string]json.RawMessage
   281→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rawSettings); err != nil {
   282→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse settings.json: %w", err)
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	// rawHooks preserves unknown hook types (e.g., "Notification", "SubagentStop")
   286→	var rawHooks map[string]json.RawMessage
   287→	if hooksRaw, ok := rawSettings["hooks"]; ok {
   288→		if err := json.Unmarshal(hooksRaw, &rawHooks); err != nil {
   289→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hooks: %w", err)
   290→		}
   291→	}
   292→	if rawHooks == nil {
   293→		rawHooks = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
   294→	}
   295→
   296→	// Parse only the hook types we need to modify
   297→	var sessionStart, sessionEnd, stop, userPromptSubmit, preToolUse, postToolUse []ClaudeHookMatcher
   298→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "SessionStart", &sessionStart)
   299→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "SessionEnd", &sessionEnd)
   300→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "Stop", &stop)
   301→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "UserPromptSubmit", &userPromptSubmit)
   302→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", &preToolUse)
   303→	parseHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", &postToolUse)
   304→
   305→	// Remove Entire hooks from all hook types
   306→	sessionStart = removeEntireHooks(sessionStart)
   307→	sessionEnd = removeEntireHooks(sessionEnd)
   308→	stop = removeEntireHooks(stop)
   309→	userPromptSubmit = removeEntireHooks(userPromptSubmit)
   310→	preToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(preToolUse)
   311→	postToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(postToolUse)
   312→
   313→	// Marshal modified hook types back to rawHooks
   314→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SessionStart", sessionStart)
   315→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SessionEnd", sessionEnd)
   316→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "Stop", stop)
   317→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "UserPromptSubmit", userPromptSubmit)
   318→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", preToolUse)
   319→	marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", postToolUse)
   320→
   321→	// Also remove the metadata deny rule from permissions
   322→	var rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage
   323→	if permRaw, ok := rawSettings["permissions"]; ok {
   324→		if err := json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions); err != nil {
   325→			// If parsing fails, just skip permissions cleanup
   326→			rawPermissions = nil
   327→		}
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	if rawPermissions != nil {
   331→		if denyRaw, ok := rawPermissions["deny"]; ok {
   332→			var denyRules []string
   333→			if err := json.Unmarshal(denyRaw, &denyRules); err == nil {
   334→				// Filter out the metadata deny rule
   335→				filteredRules := make([]string, 0, len(denyRules))
   336→				for _, rule := range denyRules {
   337→					if rule != metadataDenyRule {
   338→						filteredRules = append(filteredRules, rule)
   339→					}
   340→				}
   341→				if len(filteredRules) > 0 {
   342→					denyJSON, err := json.Marshal(filteredRules)
   343→					if err == nil {
   344→						rawPermissions["deny"] = denyJSON
   345→					}
   346→				} else {
   347→					// Remove empty deny array
   348→					delete(rawPermissions, "deny")
   349→				}
   350→			}
   351→		}
   352→
   353→		// If permissions is empty, remove it entirely
   354→		if len(rawPermissions) > 0 {
   355→			permJSON, err := json.Marshal(rawPermissions)
   356→			if err == nil {
   357→				rawSettings["permissions"] = permJSON
   358→			}
   359→		} else {
   360→			delete(rawSettings, "permissions")
   361→		}
   362→	}
   363→
   364→	// Marshal hooks back (preserving unknown hook types)
   365→	if len(rawHooks) > 0 {
   366→		hooksJSON, err := json.Marshal(rawHooks)
   367→		if err != nil {
   368→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal hooks: %w", err)
   369→		}
   370→		rawSettings["hooks"] = hooksJSON
   371→	} else {
   372→		delete(rawSettings, "hooks")
   373→	}
   374→
   375→	// Write back
   376→	output, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(rawSettings, "", "  ")
   377→	if err != nil {
   378→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal settings: %w", err)
   379→	}
   380→	if err := os.WriteFile(settingsPath, output, 0o600); err != nil {
   381→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write settings.json: %w", err)
   382→	}
   383→	return nil
   384→}

   386→// AreHooksInstalled checks if Entire hooks are installed.
   387→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) AreHooksInstalled() bool {
   388→	// Use repo root to find .claude directory when run from a subdirectory
   389→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   390→	if err != nil {
   391→		repoRoot = "." // Fallback to CWD if not in a git repo
   392→	}
   393→	settingsPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".claude", ClaudeSettingsFileName)
   394→	data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath) //nolint:gosec // path is constructed from repo root + fixed path
   395→	if err != nil {
   396→		return false
   397→	}
   398→
   399→	var settings ClaudeSettings
   400→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &settings); err != nil {
   401→		return false
   402→	}
   403→
   404→	// Check for at least one of our hooks (new or old format)
   405→	return hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "entire hooks claude-code stop") ||
   406→		hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "go run ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/cmd/entire/main.go hooks claude-code stop") ||
   407→		// Backwards compatibility: check for old hook formats
   408→		hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "entire hooks claudecode stop") ||
   409→		hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "go run ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/cmd/entire/main.go hooks claudecode stop") ||
   410→		hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "entire rewind claude-hook --stop") ||
   411→		hookCommandExists(settings.Hooks.Stop, "go run ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/cmd/entire/main.go rewind claude-hook --stop")
   412→}

   426→// Helper functions for hook management
   427→
   428→func hookCommandExists(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, command string) bool {
   429→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   430→		for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
   431→			if hook.Command == command {
   432→				return true
   433→			}
   434→		}
   435→	}
   436→	return false
   437→}
   438→
   439→func hookCommandExistsWithMatcher(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, matcherName, command string) bool {
   440→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   441→		if matcher.Matcher == matcherName {
   442→			for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
   443→				if hook.Command == command {
   444→					return true
   445→				}
   446→			}
   447→		}
   448→	}
   449→	return false
   450→}
   451→
   452→func addHookToMatcher(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, matcherName, command string) []ClaudeHookMatcher {
   453→	entry := ClaudeHookEntry{
   454→		Type:    "command",
   455→		Command: command,
   456→	}
   457→
   458→	// If no matcher name, add to a matcher with empty string
   459→	if matcherName == "" {
   460→		for i, matcher := range matchers {
   461→			if matcher.Matcher == "" {
   462→				matchers[i].Hooks = append(matchers[i].Hooks, entry)
   463→				return matchers
   464→			}
   465→		}
   466→		return append(matchers, ClaudeHookMatcher{
   467→			Matcher: "",
   468→			Hooks:   []ClaudeHookEntry{entry},
   469→		})
   470→	}
   471→
   472→	// Find or create matcher with the given name
   473→	for i, matcher := range matchers {
   474→		if matcher.Matcher == matcherName {
   475→			matchers[i].Hooks = append(matchers[i].Hooks, entry)
   476→			return matchers
   477→		}
   478→	}
   479→
   480→	return append(matchers, ClaudeHookMatcher{
   481→		Matcher: matcherName,
   482→		Hooks:   []ClaudeHookEntry{entry},
   483→	})
   484→}
   485→
   486→// isEntireHook checks if a command is an Entire hook (old or new format)
   487→func isEntireHook(command string) bool {
   488→	for _, prefix := range entireHookPrefixes {
   489→		if strings.HasPrefix(command, prefix) {
   490→			return true
   491→		}
   492→	}
   493→	return false
   494→}
   495→
   496→// removeEntireHooks removes all Entire hooks from a list of matchers (for simple hooks like Stop)
   497→func removeEntireHooks(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher) []ClaudeHookMatcher {
   498→	result := make([]ClaudeHookMatcher, 0, len(matchers))
   499→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   500→		filteredHooks := make([]ClaudeHookEntry, 0, len(matcher.Hooks))
   501→		for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
   502→			if !isEntireHook(hook.Command) {
   503→				filteredHooks = append(filteredHooks, hook)
   504→			}
   505→		}
   506→		// Only keep the matcher if it has hooks remaining
   507→		if len(filteredHooks) > 0 {
   508→			matcher.Hooks = filteredHooks
   509→			result = append(result, matcher)
   510→		}
   511→	}
   512→	return result
   513→}
   514→
   515→// removeEntireHooksFromMatchers removes Entire hooks from tool-use matchers (PreToolUse, PostToolUse)
   516→// This handles the nested structure where hooks are grouped by tool matcher (e.g., "Task", "TodoWrite")
   517→func removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher) []ClaudeHookMatcher {
   518→	// Same logic as removeEntireHooks - both work on the same structure
   519→	return removeEntireHooks(matchers)
   520→}
```

```
    25→	t.Parallel()
    26→
    27→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
    28→
    29→	// Count commits before
    30→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
    31→	t.Logf("Commits before: %d", commitsBefore)
    32→
    33→	// Agent creates multiple files and commits them separately
    34→	granularCommitPrompt := `Please do the following tasks, committing after each one:
    35→
    36→1. Create a file called file1.go with this content:
    37→   package main
    38→   func One() int { return 1 }
    39→   Then run: git add file1.go && git commit -m "Add file1"
    40→
    41→2. Create a file called file2.go with this content:
    42→   package main
    43→   func Two() int { return 2 }
    44→   Then run: git add file2.go && git commit -m "Add file2"
    45→
    46→3. Create a file called file3.go with this content:
    47→   package main
    48→   func Three() int { return 3 }
    49→   Then run: git add file3.go && git commit -m "Add file3"
    50→
    51→Do each task in order, making the commit after each file creation.`
    52→
    53→	result, err := env.RunAgentWithTools(granularCommitPrompt, []string{"Write", "Bash"})
    54→	require.NoError(t, err)
    55→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
    56→	t.Logf("Agent output: %s", result.Stdout)
    57→
    58→	// Verify all files were created
    59→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("file1.go"), "file1.go should exist")
    60→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("file2.go"), "file2.go should exist")
    61→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("file3.go"), "file3.go should exist")
    62→
    63→	// Verify multiple commits were made
    64→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
    65→	t.Logf("Commits after: %d", commitsAfter)
    66→	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, commitsAfter-commitsBefore, 3, "Should have at least 3 new commits")
    67→
    68→	// Get all checkpoint IDs from history
    69→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
    70→	t.Logf("Found %d checkpoint IDs in commit history", len(checkpointIDs))
    71→	for i, id := range checkpointIDs {
    72→		t.Logf("  Checkpoint %d: %s", i, id)
    73→	}
    74→
    75→	// Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID (1:1 model)
    76→	if len(checkpointIDs) >= 3 {
    77→		// Verify checkpoint IDs are unique
    78→		idSet := make(map[string]bool)
    79→		for _, id := range checkpointIDs {
    80→			require.Falsef(t, idSet[id], "Checkpoint IDs should be unique: %s is duplicated", id)
    81→			idSet[id] = true
    82→		}
    83→	}
    84→
    85→	// Verify metadata branch exists
    86→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
    87→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
    88→
    89→	// Validate each checkpoint has proper metadata and content
    90→	// Note: checkpointIDs are in reverse chronological order (newest first)
    91→	// So checkpointIDs[0] = file3.go, [1] = file2.go, [2] = file1.go
    92→	//
    93→	// With deferred finalization, all checkpoints from the same turn get the
    94→	// FULL transcript at turn end, so all checkpoints should contain all file names.
    95→	allFiles := []string{"file1.go", "file2.go", "file3.go"}
    96→	for i, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
    97→		fileNum := len(checkpointIDs) - i // Reverse the index to match file numbers
    98→		fileName := fmt.Sprintf("file%d.go", fileNum)
    99→		t.Logf("Validating checkpoint %d: %s (files_touched: %s)", i, cpID, fileName)
   100→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   101→			CheckpointID:              cpID,
   102→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   103→			FilesTouched:              []string{fileName},
   104→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: allFiles, // All checkpoints have full transcript
   105→		})
   106→	}
   107→}
```
