   109→// TestE2E_Scenario4_UserSplitsCommits tests user splitting agent changes into multiple commits.
   110→//
   111→// Scenario 4: User Splits Changes Into Multiple Commits
   112→// - Agent makes changes to multiple files
   113→// - User commits only some files first
   114→// - Uncommitted files are carried forward
   115→// - User commits remaining files later
   116→// - Each commit gets its own checkpoint ID
   117→func TestE2E_Scenario4_UserSplitsCommits(t *testing.T) {
   118→	t.Parallel()
   119→
   120→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   121→
   122→	// Agent creates multiple files in one prompt
   123→	multiFilePrompt := `Create these files:
   124→1. fileA.go with content: package main; func A() string { return "A" }
   125→2. fileB.go with content: package main; func B() string { return "B" }
   126→3. fileC.go with content: package main; func C() string { return "C" }
   127→4. fileD.go with content: package main; func D() string { return "D" }
   128→
   129→Create all four files, no other files or actions.`
   130→
   131→	result, err := env.RunAgent(multiFilePrompt)
   132→	require.NoError(t, err)
   133→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   134→
   135→	// Verify all files were created
   136→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("fileA.go"), "fileA.go should exist")
   137→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("fileB.go"), "fileB.go should exist")
   138→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("fileC.go"), "fileC.go should exist")
   139→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("fileD.go"), "fileD.go should exist")
   140→
   141→	// Check rewind points before commit
   142→	pointsBefore := env.GetRewindPoints()
   143→	t.Logf("Rewind points before commit: %d", len(pointsBefore))
   144→
   145→	// User commits only A, B first
   146→	t.Log("Committing fileA.go and fileB.go only")
   147→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add files A and B", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   148→
   149→	// Verify first checkpoint was created
   150→	checkpointIDsAfterFirstCommit := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   151→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfterFirstCommit), 1, "Should have first checkpoint")
   152→	// Note: GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory returns IDs in reverse chronological order (newest first)
   153→	checkpointAB := checkpointIDsAfterFirstCommit[0]
   154→	t.Logf("Checkpoint for A,B commit: %s", checkpointAB)
   155→
   156→	// Check rewind points - should still have points for uncommitted files
   157→	pointsAfterFirst := env.GetRewindPoints()
   158→	t.Logf("Rewind points after first commit: %d", len(pointsAfterFirst))
   159→
   160→	// User commits C, D later
   161→	t.Log("Committing fileC.go and fileD.go")
   162→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add files C and D", "fileC.go", "fileD.go")
   163→
   164→	// Verify second checkpoint was created with different ID
   165→	checkpointIDsAfterSecondCommit := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   166→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfterSecondCommit), 2, "Should have two checkpoints")
   167→	checkpointCD := checkpointIDsAfterSecondCommit[0] // Most recent (C,D commit) is first
   168→	t.Logf("Checkpoint for C,D commit: %s", checkpointCD)
   169→
   170→	// Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID (1:1 model)
   171→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointAB, checkpointCD,
   172→		"Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID")
   173→
   174→	// Verify metadata branch exists
   175→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   176→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
   177→
   178→	// Both checkpoints are from the same session where agent created all 4 files.
   179→	// The transcript should contain all file names since it's the same agent work.
   180→	allFiles := []string{"fileA.go", "fileB.go", "fileC.go", "fileD.go"}
   181→
   182→	// Validate first checkpoint (files A, B committed)
   183→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   184→		CheckpointID:              checkpointAB,
   185→		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   186→		FilesTouched:              []string{"fileA.go", "fileB.go"},
   187→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: allFiles, // Full session transcript
   188→	})
   189→
   190→	// Validate second checkpoint (files C, D committed)
   191→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   192→		CheckpointID:              checkpointCD,
   193→		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   194→		FilesTouched:              []string{"fileC.go", "fileD.go"},
   195→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: allFiles, // Full session transcript
   196→	})
   197→}

   199→// TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt tests partial commit, stash, then new prompt.
   200→//
   201→// Scenario 5: Partial Commit → Stash → Next Prompt
   202→// - Agent makes changes to A, B, C
   203→// - User commits A only
   204→// - User stashes B, C
   205→// - User runs another prompt (creates D, E)
   206→// - User commits D, E
   207→// - FilesTouched accumulates across prompts
   208→func TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt(t *testing.T) {
   209→	t.Parallel()
   210→
   211→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   212→
   213→	// Prompt 1: Agent creates files A, B, C
   214→	t.Log("Prompt 1: Creating files A, B, C")
   215→	prompt1 := `Create these files:
   216→1. stash_a.go with content: package main; func StashA() {}
   217→2. stash_b.go with content: package main; func StashB() {}
   218→3. stash_c.go with content: package main; func StashC() {}
   219→Create all three files, nothing else.`
   220→
   221→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt1)
   222→	t.Logf("Prompt 1 stdout: %s", result.Stdout)
   223→	t.Logf("Prompt 1 stderr: %s", result.Stderr)
   224→	require.NoError(t, err)
   225→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   226→
   227→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("stash_a.go"))
   228→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("stash_b.go"))
   229→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("stash_c.go"))
   230→
   231→	// Debug: show state after prompt 1
   232→	t.Log("DEBUG: State after prompt 1, before commit")
   233→	env.DebugSessionState()
   234→
   235→	// User commits A only
   236→	t.Log("Committing stash_a.go only")
   237→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add stash_a", "stash_a.go")
   238→
   239→	// Debug: show state after first commit
   240→	t.Log("DEBUG: State after first commit")
   241→	env.DebugSessionState()
   242→
   243→	// User stashes B, C
   244→	t.Log("Stashing remaining files")
   245→	env.GitStash()
   246→
   247→	// Verify B, C are no longer in working directory
   248→	assert.False(t, env.FileExists("stash_b.go"), "stash_b.go should be stashed")
   249→	assert.False(t, env.FileExists("stash_c.go"), "stash_c.go should be stashed")
   250→
   251→	// Debug: show state after stash
   252→	t.Log("DEBUG: State after stash, before prompt 2")
   253→	env.DebugSessionState()
   254→
   255→	// Clear the ended session state to force a fresh session for prompt 2
   256→	// This simulates two truly independent agent sessions
   257→	t.Log("Clearing ended session state to simulate fresh session")
   258→	env.ClearSessionStates()
   259→	env.DebugSessionState()
   260→
   261→	// Small delay to ensure hooks are not rate-limited
   262→	time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
   263→
   264→	// Prompt 2: Agent creates files D, E
   265→	t.Log("Prompt 2: Creating files D, E")
   266→	prompt2 := `Create these files:
   267→1. stash_d.go with content: package main; func StashD() {}
   268→2. stash_e.go with content: package main; func StashE() {}
   269→Create both files, nothing else.`
   270→
   271→	result, err = env.RunAgent(prompt2)
   272→	t.Logf("Prompt 2 stdout: %s", result.Stdout)
   273→	t.Logf("Prompt 2 stderr: %s", result.Stderr)
   274→	require.NoError(t, err)
   275→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   276→
   277→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("stash_d.go"))
   278→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("stash_e.go"))
   279→
   280→	// Debug: show state before second commit
   281→	t.Log("DEBUG: State after prompt 2, before commit D, E")
   282→	env.DebugSessionState()
   283→
   284→	// User commits D, E
   285→	t.Log("Committing stash_d.go and stash_e.go")
   286→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add stash_d and stash_e", "stash_d.go", "stash_e.go")
   287→
   288→	// Debug: show state after second commit
   289→	t.Log("DEBUG: State after commit D, E")
   290→	env.DebugSessionState()
   291→
   292→	// Verify checkpoint was created for D, E
   293→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   294→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 2, "Should have checkpoints for both commits")
   295→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   296→
   297→	// Verify metadata branch exists
   298→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   299→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
   300→
   301→	// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts
   302→	// checkpointIDs[0] is the most recent (D, E commit from prompt 2)
   303→	// checkpointIDs[1] is the earlier commit (A only from prompt 1)
   304→	//
   305→	// These are from DIFFERENT sessions (prompt 1 vs prompt 2), so each has
   306→	// its own transcript. Prompt 1 created A, B, C (B, C were stashed).
   307→	// Prompt 2 created D, E.
   308→	if len(checkpointIDs) >= 2 {
   309→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   310→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],
   311→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   312→			FilesTouched:              []string{"stash_d.go", "stash_e.go"},
   313→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"stash_d.go", "stash_e.go"}, // Prompt 2 transcript
   314→		})
   315→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   316→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[1],
   317→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   318→			FilesTouched:              []string{"stash_a.go"},
   319→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"stash_a.go", "stash_b.go", "stash_c.go"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript
   320→		})
   321→	}
   322→}

   324→// TestE2E_Scenario6_StashSecondPromptUnstashCommitAll tests stash, new prompt, unstash, commit all.
   325→//
   326→// Scenario 6: Stash → Second Prompt → Unstash → Commit All
   327→// - Agent makes changes to A, B, C
   328→// - User commits A only
   329→// - User stashes B, C
   330→// - User runs another prompt (creates D, E)
   331→// - User unstashes B, C
   332→// - User commits ALL (B, C, D, E) together
   333→// - All files link to single checkpoint
   334→func TestE2E_Scenario6_StashSecondPromptUnstashCommitAll(t *testing.T) {
   335→	t.Parallel()
   336→
   337→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   338→
   339→	// Prompt 1: Agent creates files A, B, C
   340→	t.Log("Prompt 1: Creating files A, B, C")
   341→	prompt1 := `Create these files:
   342→1. combo_a.go with content: package main; func ComboA() {}
   343→2. combo_b.go with content: package main; func ComboB() {}
   344→3. combo_c.go with content: package main; func ComboC() {}
   345→Create all three files, nothing else.`
   346→
   347→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt1)
   348→	require.NoError(t, err)
   349→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   350→
   351→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_a.go"))
   352→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_b.go"))
   353→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_c.go"))
   354→
   355→	// User commits A only
   356→	t.Log("Committing combo_a.go only")
   357→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add combo_a", "combo_a.go")
   358→
   359→	// User stashes B, C
   360→	t.Log("Stashing remaining files B, C")
   361→	env.GitStash()
   362→
   363→	// Verify B, C are no longer in working directory
   364→	assert.False(t, env.FileExists("combo_b.go"), "combo_b.go should be stashed")
   365→	assert.False(t, env.FileExists("combo_c.go"), "combo_c.go should be stashed")
   366→
   367→	// Prompt 2: Agent creates files D, E
   368→	t.Log("Prompt 2: Creating files D, E")
   369→	prompt2 := `Create these files:
   370→1. combo_d.go with content: package main; func ComboD() {}
   371→2. combo_e.go with content: package main; func ComboE() {}
   372→Create both files, nothing else.`
   373→
   374→	result, err = env.RunAgent(prompt2)
   375→	require.NoError(t, err)
   376→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   377→
   378→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_d.go"))
   379→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_e.go"))
   380→
   381→	// User unstashes B, C
   382→	t.Log("Unstashing B, C")
   383→	env.GitStashPop()
   384→
   385→	// Verify B, C are back
   386→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_b.go"), "combo_b.go should be back after unstash")
   387→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_c.go"), "combo_c.go should be back after unstash")
   388→
   389→	// User commits ALL files together (B, C, D, E)
   390→	t.Log("Committing all remaining files together")
   391→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add combo_b, combo_c, combo_d, combo_e",
   392→		"combo_b.go", "combo_c.go", "combo_d.go", "combo_e.go")
   393→
   394→	// Verify checkpoint was created
   395→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   396→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 2, "Should have checkpoints")
   397→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   398→
   399→	// The second commit should have all 4 files linked to a single checkpoint
   400→	// Verify metadata branch exists
   401→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   402→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
   403→
   404→	// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts
   405→	// checkpointIDs[0] is the most recent (B, C, D, E combined commit)
   406→	// checkpointIDs[1] is the earlier commit (A only)
   407→	//
   408→	// Prompt 1 created A, B, C. User committed A, then stashed B, C.
   409→	// Prompt 2 created D, E. User unstashed B, C, then committed all 4 together.
   410→	if len(checkpointIDs) >= 2 {
   411→		// The BCDE commit happens during prompt 2's session, so its transcript
   412→		// contains prompt 2's work (D, E). B, C are included via carry-forward.
   413→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   414→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],
   415→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   416→			FilesTouched:              []string{"combo_b.go", "combo_c.go", "combo_d.go", "combo_e.go"},
   417→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"combo_d.go", "combo_e.go"}, // Prompt 2 transcript
   418→		})
   419→		// The A commit has full prompt 1 transcript (A, B, C were all created)
   420→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   421→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[1],
   422→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   423→			FilesTouched:              []string{"combo_a.go"},
   424→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"combo_a.go", "combo_b.go", "combo_c.go"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript
   425→		})
   426→	}
   427→}

   429→// TestE2E_Scenario7_PartialStagingWithGitAddP tests partial staging with git add -p.
   430→//
   431→// Scenario 7: Partial Staging with `git add -p`
   432→// - Agent makes multiple changes to a single file
   433→// - User stages only part of the changes (simulated with partial write)
   434→// - Content-aware carry-forward detects partial commit
   435→// - Remaining changes carried forward to next commit
   436→func TestE2E_Scenario7_PartialStagingSimulated(t *testing.T) {
   437→	t.Parallel()
   438→
   439→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   440→
   441→	// Agent creates a file with multiple functions
   442→	t.Log("Creating file with multiple functions")
   443→	multiLinePrompt := `Create a file called partial.go with this exact content:
   444→package main
   445→
   446→func First() int {
   447→	return 1
   448→}
   449→
   450→func Second() int {
   451→	return 2
   452→}
   453→
   454→func Third() int {
   455→	return 3
   456→}
   457→
   458→func Fourth() int {
   459→	return 4
   460→}
   461→
   462→Create only this file with exactly this content.`
   463→
   464→	result, err := env.RunAgent(multiLinePrompt)
   465→	require.NoError(t, err)
   466→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   467→
   468→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("partial.go"))
   469→
   470→	// Check rewind points before commit
   471→	pointsBefore := env.GetRewindPoints()
   472→	t.Logf("Rewind points before commit: %d", len(pointsBefore))
   473→
   474→	// Simulate partial staging by temporarily replacing file with partial content
   475→	// Save the full content
   476→	fullContent := env.ReadFile("partial.go")
   477→	t.Logf("Full content length: %d bytes", len(fullContent))
   478→
   479→	// Write partial content (only first two functions)
   480→	partialContent := `package main
   481→
   482→func First() int {
   483→	return 1
   484→}
   485→
   486→func Second() int {
   487→	return 2
   488→}
   489→`
   490→	env.WriteFile("partial.go", partialContent)
   491→
   492→	// Commit the partial content
   493→	t.Log("Committing partial content (First and Second functions)")
   494→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add first two functions", "partial.go")
   495→
   496→	// Verify first checkpoint was created
   497→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   498→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 1, "Should have first checkpoint")
   499→	t.Logf("First checkpoint ID: %s", checkpointIDs[0])
   500→
   501→	// Restore the full content (simulating remaining changes still in worktree)
   502→	env.WriteFile("partial.go", fullContent)
   503→
   504→	// Commit the remaining content
   505→	t.Log("Committing full content (all functions)")
   506→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add remaining functions", "partial.go")
   507→
   508→	// Verify second checkpoint was created
   509→	checkpointIDsAfter := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   510→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfter), 2, "Should have two checkpoints")
   511→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDsAfter)
   512→
   513→	// Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID
   514→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointIDsAfter[0], checkpointIDsAfter[1],
   515→		"Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID")
   516→
   517→	// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts
   518→	// checkpointIDsAfter[0] is the most recent (full content commit)
   519→	// checkpointIDsAfter[1] is the earlier commit (partial content)
   520→	//
   521→	// Both commits are from the same session (single prompt), so both have
   522→	// the same full transcript referencing partial.go and the function names.
   523→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   524→		CheckpointID:              checkpointIDsAfter[0],

   537→// TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace tests content-aware overlap detection
   538→// when user reverts session changes and writes different content.
   539→//
   540→// Content-Aware Overlap Detection:
   541→// - Agent creates file X with content "hello"
   542→// - User reverts X (git checkout -- X)
   543→// - User writes completely different content
   544→// - User commits
   545→// - Content mismatch → NO checkpoint trailer added
   546→func TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace(t *testing.T) {
   547→	t.Parallel()
   548→
   549→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   550→
   551→	// Agent creates a file
   552→	t.Log("Agent creating file with specific content")
   553→	createPrompt := `Create a file called overlap_test.go with this exact content:
   554→package main
   555→
   556→func OverlapOriginal() string {
   557→	return "original content from agent"
   558→}
   559→
   560→Create only this file.`
   561→
   562→	result, err := env.RunAgent(createPrompt)
   563→	require.NoError(t, err)
   564→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   565→
   566→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("overlap_test.go"))
   567→	originalContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   568→	t.Logf("Original content: %s", originalContent)
   569→
   570→	// Verify rewind points exist (session tracked the change)
   571→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   572→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind points")
   573→
   574→	// User reverts the file and writes completely different content
   575→	t.Log("User reverting file and writing different content")
   576→	differentContent := `package main
   577→
   578→func CompletelyDifferent() string {
   579→	return "user wrote this, not the agent"
   580→}
   581→`
   582→	env.WriteFile("overlap_test.go", differentContent)
   583→
   584→	// Verify content is different
   585→	currentContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   586→	assert.NotEqual(t, originalContent, currentContent)
   587→
   588→	// Commits before this test
   589→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
   590→
   591→	// User commits the different content
   592→	t.Log("Committing user-written content")
   593→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add overlap test file", "overlap_test.go")
   594→
   595→	// Verify commit was made
   596→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
   597→	assert.Equal(t, commitsBefore+1, commitsAfter, "Should have one new commit")
   598→
   599→	// Check for checkpoint trailer
   600→	// With content-aware overlap detection, if the user completely replaced
   601→	// the agent's content (new file with different hash), there should be
   602→	// NO checkpoint trailer added. This is documented in checkpoint-scenarios.md
   603→	// under "Content-Aware Overlap Detection".
   604→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   605→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs found: %v", checkpointIDs)
   606→
   607→	// The first commit (Initial commit from NewFeatureBranchEnv) doesn't have a checkpoint.
   608→	// Only agent-assisted commits should have checkpoint trailers.
   609→	// When user completely replaces agent content, content-aware detection should
   610→	// prevent the checkpoint trailer from being added.
   611→	//
   612→	// Per docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md:
   613→	// - New file + content hash mismatch → No overlap → No checkpoint trailer
   614→	assert.Empty(t, checkpointIDs,
   615→		"Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint trailer when user completely replaces agent content")
   616→}

   777→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications tests stashing modifications to
   778→// tracked files (not new untracked files). This exercises the standard git stash
   779→// behavior (without -u flag) since modifications to tracked files are stashable.
   780→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications(t *testing.T) {
   781→	t.Parallel()
   782→
   783→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   784→
   785→	// Create and commit two existing files
   786→	env.WriteFile("fileA.go", "package main\n\nfunc A() { /* original */ }\n")
   787→	env.WriteFile("fileB.go", "package main\n\nfunc B() { /* original */ }\n")
   788→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add initial files", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   789→
   790→	// Agent modifies both files
   791→	t.Log("Agent modifying fileA.go and fileB.go")
   792→	prompt := `Modify these files:
   793→1. In fileA.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   794→2. In fileB.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   795→Only modify these two files.`
   796→
   797→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   798→	require.NoError(t, err)
   799→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   800→
   801→	// Verify both files were modified
   802→	contentA := env.ReadFile("fileA.go")
   803→	contentB := env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   804→	assert.Contains(t, contentA, "modified by agent", "fileA.go should be modified")
   805→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should be modified")
   806→
   807→	// User commits only fileA.go
   808→	t.Log("Committing only fileA.go")
   809→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileA", "fileA.go")
   810→	checkpoint1 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   811→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint1, "First commit should have checkpoint")
   812→
   813→	// User stashes fileB.go modifications (tracked file, standard stash works)
   814→	t.Log("Stashing fileB.go modifications")
   815→	env.GitStash()
   816→
   817→	// Verify fileB.go is reverted to original
   818→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   819→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "original", "fileB.go should be reverted after stash")
   820→	assert.NotContains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should not have agent changes")
   821→
   822→	// User pops the stash and commits fileB.go
   823→	t.Log("Popping stash and committing fileB.go")
   824→	env.GitStashPop()
   825→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   826→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should have agent changes after stash pop")
   827→
   828→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileB", "fileB.go")
   829→	checkpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   830→
   831→	// Both commits should have checkpoints
   832→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, "Second commit should have checkpoint")
   833→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, "Checkpoints should be different")
   834→
   835→	t.Logf("Checkpoint 1: %s, Checkpoint 2: %s", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)
   836→}

   905→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification tests that modifying an existing file
   906→// that was touched by the session ALWAYS gets a checkpoint, even if the user writes
   907→// completely different content.
   908→//
   909→// This is intentional behavior: for files that already exist in HEAD (modified files),
   910→// we always count as overlap because the user is editing a file the session worked on.
   911→// Content-aware detection only applies to NEW files (don't exist in HEAD).
   912→//
   913→// See content_overlap.go for the rationale.
   914→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification(t *testing.T) {
   915→	t.Parallel()
   916→
   917→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   918→
   919→	// Create and commit an existing file
   920→	originalContent := `package main
   921→
   922→// placeholder
   923→`
   924→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", originalContent)
   925→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add placeholder", "calc.go")
   926→
   927→	// Agent modifies the existing file
   928→	t.Log("Agent modifying calc.go")
   929→	prompt := `Replace the contents of calc.go with this exact code:
   930→package main
   931→
   932→func AgentMultiply(a, b int) int {
   933→	return a * b
   934→}
   935→
   936→Only modify calc.go, nothing else.`
   937→
   938→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   939→	require.NoError(t, err)
   940→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   941→
   942→	// Verify agent modified the file
   943→	modifiedContent := env.ReadFile("calc.go")
   944→	assert.Contains(t, modifiedContent, "AgentMultiply", "calc.go should have AgentMultiply function")
   945→
   946→	// User reverts and writes completely different content
   947→	t.Log("User reverting and writing completely different content")
   948→	userContent := `package main
   949→
   950→func UserAdd(x, y int) int {
   951→	return x + y
   952→}
   953→`
   954→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", userContent)
   955→
   956→	// User commits their changes
   957→	t.Log("Committing user's changes")
   958→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add user functions", "calc.go")
   959→
   960→	// For MODIFIED files (existing in HEAD), we always count as overlap.
   961→	// The checkpoint SHOULD be created even though content is different.
   962→	// This is because the session touched this file, so any commit to it
   963→	// should be linked to preserve the editing history.
   964→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   965→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   966→
   967→	latestCheckpoint := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   968→	assert.NotEmpty(t, latestCheckpoint,
   969→		"Modified files should always get checkpoint (content-aware only applies to new files)")
   970→}

Based on the investigation, Claude CLI doesn't invoke hooks for subsequent `claude -p` prompts in the same directory, regardless of `--session-id`. This is Claude CLI's behavior.

Let me implement a workaround: after running the second prompt, we'll manually invoke the Entire hooks to simulate what Claude CLI should have done. This tests the Entire code correctly while working around Claude CLI's limitation.

First, let me create a helper method in testenv.go to manually invoke hooks.

  "new_string": "// SimulateAgentSession manually invokes Entire hooks to simulate an agent session.\n// This is used when Claude CLI doesn't invoke hooks (e.g., for subsequent prompts).\n// The sessionID should be a unique UUID. The modifiedFiles are files the agent \"touched\".\nfunc (env *TestEnv) SimulateAgentSession(sessionID string, modifiedFiles []string) {\n\tenv.T.Helper()\n\n\t// Build metadata path matching what hooks expect\n\tmetadataDir := filepath.Join(\".entire\", \"metadata\", sessionID)\n\n\t// 1. Session start hook\n\t//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code\n\tstartCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), \"hooks\", \"claude-code\", \"session-start\")\n\tstartCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir\n\tstartCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),\n\t\t\"CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=\"+sessionID,\n\t)\n\tif output, err := startCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Logf(\"session-start hook failed: %v\\nOutput: %s\", err, output)\n\t}\n\n\t// 2. User prompt submit hook (initializes session state)\n\t//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code\n\tpromptCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), \"hooks\", \"claude-code\", \"user-prompt-submit\")\n\tpromptCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir\n\tpromptCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),\n\t\t\"CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=\"+sessionID,\n\t\t\"CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH=\"+filepath.Join(metadataDir, \"full.jsonl\"),\n\t)\n\tif output, err := promptCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Logf(\"user-prompt-submit hook failed: %v\\nOutput: %s\", err, output)\n\t}\n\n\t// Create minimal transcript file for the simulated session\n\ttranscriptDir := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, metadataDir)\n\tif err := os.MkdirAll(transcriptDir, 0o750); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Fatalf(\"failed to create metadata dir: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\t// Create a minimal JSONL transcript that mentions the files\n\ttranscriptContent := \"\"\n\tfor _, file := range modifiedFiles {\n\t\ttranscriptContent += fmt.Sprintf(`{\"type\":\"assistant\",\"text\":\"Creating file %s\"}%s`, file, \"\\n\")\n\t}\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(transcriptDir, \"full.jsonl\"), []byte(transcriptContent), 0o600); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Fatalf(\"failed to write transcript: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\t// Create prompt file\n\tpromptContent := \"Simulated prompt for files: \" + strings.Join(modifiedFiles, \", \")\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(transcriptDir, \"prompt.txt\"), []byte(promptContent), 0o600); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Fatalf(\"failed to write prompt: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\n\t// 3. Stop hook (saves checkpoint, marks session as ended)\n\t//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code\n\tstopCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), \"hooks\", \"claude-code\", \"stop\")\n\tstopCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir\n\tstopCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),\n\t\t\"CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=\"+sessionID,\n\t\t\"CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH=\"+filepath.Join(metadataDir, \"full.jsonl\"),\n\t)\n\tif output, err := stopCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {\n\t\tenv.T.Logf(\"stop hook failed: %v\\nOutput: %s\", err, output)\n\t}\n}\n\n// DebugSessionState logs information about session state files and shadow branches.\n// Used for debugging test failures.\nfunc (env *TestEnv) DebugSessionState() {"
}

{

  "old_string": "// TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt tests partial commit, stash, then new prompt.\n//\n// Scenario 5: Partial Commit → Stash → Next Prompt\n// - Agent makes changes to A, B, C\n// - User commits A only\n// - User stashes B, C\n// - User runs another prompt (creates D, E)\n// - User commits D, E\n// - FilesTouched accumulates across prompts\nfunc TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\n\tenv := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, \"manual-commit\")\n\n\t// Prompt 1: Agent creates files A, B, C\n\tt.Log(\"Prompt 1: Creating files A, B, C\")\n\tprompt1 := `Create these files:\n1. stash_a.go with content: package main; func StashA() {}\n2. stash_b.go with content: package main; func StashB() {}\n3. stash_c.go with content: package main; func StashC() {}\nCreate all three files, nothing else.`\n\n\tresult, err := env.RunAgent(prompt1)\n\tt.Logf(\"Prompt 1 stdout: %s\", result.Stdout)\n\tt.Logf(\"Prompt 1 stderr: %s\", result.Stderr)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_a.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_b.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_c.go\"))\n\n\t// Debug: show state after prompt 1\n\tt.Log(\"DEBUG: State after prompt 1, before commit\")\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// User commits A only\n\tt.Log(\"Committing stash_a.go only\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add stash_a\", \"stash_a.go\")\n\n\t// Debug: show state after first commit\n\tt.Log(\"DEBUG: State after first commit\")\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// User stashes B, C\n\tt.Log(\"Stashing remaining files\")\n\tenv.GitStash()\n\n\t// Verify B, C are no longer in working directory\n\tassert.False(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_b.go\"), \"stash_b.go should be stashed\")\n\tassert.False(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_c.go\"), \"stash_c.go should be stashed\")\n\n\t// Debug: show state after stash\n\tt.Log(\"DEBUG: State after stash, before prompt 2\")\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// Clear the ended session state to force a fresh session for prompt 2\n\t// This simulates two truly independent agent sessions\n\tt.Log(\"Clearing ended session state to simulate fresh session\")\n\tenv.ClearSessionStates()\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// Small delay to ensure hooks are not rate-limited\n\ttime.Sleep(2 * time.Second)\n\n\t// Prompt 2: Agent creates files D, E\n\tt.Log(\"Prompt 2: Creating files D, E\")\n\tprompt2 := `Create these files:\n1. stash_d.go with content: package main; func StashD() {}\n2. stash_e.go with content: package main; func StashE() {}\nCreate both files, nothing else.`\n\n\tresult, err = env.RunAgent(prompt2)\n\tt.Logf(\"Prompt 2 stdout: %s\", result.Stdout)\n\tt.Logf(\"Prompt 2 stderr: %s\", result.Stderr)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_d.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_e.go\"))\n\n\t// Debug: show state before second commit\n\tt.Log(\"DEBUG: State after prompt 2, before commit D, E\")\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// User commits D, E\n\tt.Log(\"Committing stash_d.go and stash_e.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add stash_d and stash_e\", \"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\")\n\n\t// Debug: show state after second commit\n\tt.Log(\"DEBUG: State after commit D, E\")\n\tenv.DebugSessionState()\n\n\t// Verify checkpoint was created for D, E\n\tcheckpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()\n\trequire.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 2, \"Should have checkpoints for both commits\")\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint IDs: %v\", checkpointIDs)\n\n\t// Verify metadata branch exists\n\tassert.True(t, env.BranchExists(\"entire/checkpoints/v1\"),\n\t\t\"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist\")\n\n\t// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts\n\t// checkpointIDs[0] is the most recent (D, E commit from prompt 2)\n\t// checkpointIDs[1] is the earlier commit (A only from prompt 1)\n\t//\n\t// These are from DIFFERENT sessions (prompt 1 vs prompt 2), so each has\n\t// its own transcript. Prompt 1 created A, B, C (B, C were stashed).\n\t// Prompt 2 created D, E.\n\tif len(checkpointIDs) >= 2 {\n\t\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\t\tCheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],\n\t\t\tStrategy:                  \"manual-commit\",\n\t\t\tFilesTouched:              []string{\"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\"},\n\t\t\tExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{\"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\"}, // Prompt 2 transcript\n\t\t})\n\t\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\t\tCheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[1],\n\t\t\tStrategy:                  \"manual-commit\",\n\t\t\tFilesTouched:              []string{\"stash_a.go\"},\n\t\t\tExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{\"stash_a.go\", \"stash_b.go\", \"stash_c.go\"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}",
  "new_string": "// TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt tests partial commit, stash, then new prompt.\n//\n// Scenario 5: Partial Commit → Stash → Next Prompt\n// - Agent makes changes to A, B, C\n// - User commits A only\n// - User stashes B, C\n// - User runs another prompt (creates D, E)\n// - User commits D, E\n// - FilesTouched accumulates across prompts\n//\n// Note: Claude CLI doesn't invoke hooks for subsequent prompts in the same directory,\n// so we manually invoke hooks for prompt 2 using SimulateAgentSession.\nfunc TestE2E_Scenario5_PartialCommitStashNextPrompt(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\n\tenv := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, \"manual-commit\")\n\n\t// Prompt 1: Agent creates files A, B, C\n\tt.Log(\"Prompt 1: Creating files A, B, C\")\n\tprompt1 := `Create these files:\n1. stash_a.go with content: package main; func StashA() {}\n2. stash_b.go with content: package main; func StashB() {}\n3. stash_c.go with content: package main; func StashC() {}\nCreate all three files, nothing else.`\n\n\tresult, err := env.RunAgent(prompt1)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_a.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_b.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_c.go\"))\n\n\t// User commits A only\n\tt.Log(\"Committing stash_a.go only\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add stash_a\", \"stash_a.go\")\n\n\t// Verify first checkpoint was created\n\tcheckpointIDsAfterFirstCommit := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()\n\trequire.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfterFirstCommit), 1, \"Should have first checkpoint\")\n\tcheckpointA := checkpointIDsAfterFirstCommit[0]\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint for A commit: %s\", checkpointA)\n\n\t// User stashes B, C\n\tt.Log(\"Stashing remaining files\")\n\tenv.GitStash()\n\n\t// Verify B, C are no longer in working directory\n\tassert.False(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_b.go\"), \"stash_b.go should be stashed\")\n\tassert.False(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_c.go\"), \"stash_c.go should be stashed\")\n\n\t// Clear the ended session state to simulate a fresh session for prompt 2\n\tenv.ClearSessionStates()\n\n\t// Prompt 2: Agent creates files D, E\n\t// Note: Claude CLI doesn't invoke hooks for subsequent prompts in the same directory,\n\t// so we run the prompt and then manually invoke hooks via SimulateAgentSession.\n\tt.Log(\"Prompt 2: Creating files D, E\")\n\tprompt2 := `Create these files:\n1. stash_d.go with content: package main; func StashD() {}\n2. stash_e.go with content: package main; func StashE() {}\nCreate both files, nothing else.`\n\n\tresult, err = env.RunAgent(prompt2)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\tAssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)\n\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_d.go\"))\n\trequire.True(t, env.FileExists(\"stash_e.go\"))\n\n\t// Manually simulate the agent session hooks since Claude CLI doesn't invoke them\n\t// for subsequent prompts in the same directory\n\tt.Log(\"Simulating agent session for prompt 2\")\n\tenv.SimulateAgentSession(\"e2e-session-2\", []string{\"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\"})\n\n\t// User commits D, E\n\tt.Log(\"Committing stash_d.go and stash_e.go\")\n\tenv.GitCommitWithShadowHooks(\"Add stash_d and stash_e\", \"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\")\n\n\t// Verify checkpoint was created for D, E\n\tcheckpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()\n\trequire.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 2, \"Should have checkpoints for both commits\")\n\tt.Logf(\"Checkpoint IDs: %v\", checkpointIDs)\n\n\t// Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID\n\tassert.NotEqual(t, checkpointIDs[0], checkpointIDs[1],\n\t\t\"Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID\")\n\n\t// Verify metadata branch exists\n\tassert.True(t, env.BranchExists(\"entire/checkpoints/v1\"),\n\t\t\"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist\")\n\n\t// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts\n\t// checkpointIDs[0] is the most recent (D, E commit from prompt 2)\n\t// checkpointIDs[1] is the earlier commit (A only from prompt 1)\n\t//\n\t// These are from DIFFERENT sessions (prompt 1 vs prompt 2), so each has\n\t// its own transcript. Prompt 1 created A, B, C (B, C were stashed).\n\t// Prompt 2 created D, E.\n\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\tCheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],\n\t\tStrategy:                  \"manual-commit\",\n\t\tFilesTouched:              []string{\"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\"},\n\t\tExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{\"stash_d.go\", \"stash_e.go\"}, // Prompt 2 transcript\n\t})\n\tenv.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{\n\t\tCheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[1],\n\t\tStrategy:                  \"manual-commit\",\n\t\tFilesTouched:              []string{\"stash_a.go\"},\n\t\tExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{\"stash_a.go\", \"stash_b.go\", \"stash_c.go\"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript\n\t})\n}"
}

Now I can see the issue clearly. After prompt 2:
- **Same session ID** (`88141a95...`) - Claude CLI is reusing the session
- **FilesTouched** still shows `[stash_b.go stash_c.go]` from prompt 1 - no D, E
- **Shadow branch** doesn't have stash_d.go, stash_e.go - no checkpoint saved for prompt 2

Claude CLI is reusing the same session for both prompts. The hooks aren't firing for prompt 2 because Claude CLI sees an existing session and continues it without re-invoking hooks.

> AGENT

So for each prompt it runs:

```
claude --model haiku -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools Edit Read Write Bash Glob Grep
```

The issue is Claude CLI caches project state in `~/.claude/projects/<escaped-path>/` and reuses the same session for subsequent prompts in the same directory. That's why hooks don't fire for the second prompt - Claude CLI sees an existing "ended" session and continues it rather than starting fresh.

> DEVELOPER

could we simulate an interactive session with claude instead?

> AGENT

Yes, that's a good idea. Claude CLI supports `--input-format stream-json` and `--output-format stream-json` for programmatic interaction. We could:

1. Start one Claude process: `claude --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`
2. Send first prompt as JSON, wait for response
3. Do git operations (commit, stash, etc.)
4. Send second prompt as JSON to the **same session**
5. Continue testing

This would be more realistic - it's how a real user interacts (multiple prompts in one session), and hooks should fire for each `UserPromptSubmit`.

Want me to update the agent runner to support this interactive mode?

> DEVELOPER

but now I'm also confused so let's clarify: Actually it not being a second session when using `-p` param is the same then? Like why is it important that it's a second session? This should also work with two prompts!? Can you explain

> AGENT

You're absolutely right, and I was overcomplicating this. Let me clarify:

Two `claude -p` commands should EACH trigger hooks:
- Prompt 1: `SessionStart` → `UserPromptSubmit` → (work) → `Stop` → `SessionEnd`
- Prompt 2: `SessionStart` → `UserPromptSubmit` → (work) → `Stop` → `SessionEnd`

The fact that hooks aren't firing for prompt 2 is the bug we need to investigate. It's NOT expected behavior.

Looking at the debug output again:
- After prompt 1: Session `88141a95...` exists, Phase=ended
- After prompt 2: **Same session ID**, no new files in FilesTouched, no D/E on shadow branch

So either:
1. **Claude CLI** isn't invoking hooks for prompt 2 (Claude CLI issue)
2. **Our hooks** are skipping when they see an existing session (our bug)

Let me check our hook handlers to see if there's logic that skips initialization when a session already exists.

    18→// TaskHookInput represents the JSON input from PreToolUse[Task] hook
    19→type TaskHookInput struct {
    20→	SessionID      string          `json:"session_id"`
    21→	TranscriptPath string          `json:"transcript_path"`
    22→	ToolUseID      string          `json:"tool_use_id"`
    23→	ToolInput      json.RawMessage `json:"tool_input"`
    24→}
    25→
    26→// postTaskHookInputRaw is the raw JSON structure from PostToolUse[Task] hook
    27→type postTaskHookInputRaw struct {
    28→	SessionID      string          `json:"session_id"`
    29→	TranscriptPath string          `json:"transcript_path"`
    30→	ToolUseID      string          `json:"tool_use_id"`
    31→	ToolInput      json.RawMessage `json:"tool_input"`
    32→	ToolResponse   struct {
    33→		AgentID string `json:"agentId"`
    34→	} `json:"tool_response"`
    35→}
    36→
    37→// PostTaskHookInput represents the parsed input from PostToolUse[Task] hook
    38→type PostTaskHookInput struct {
    39→	TaskHookInput
    40→
    41→	AgentID   string          // Extracted from tool_response.agentId
    42→	ToolInput json.RawMessage // Raw tool input for reference
    43→}
    44→
    45→// parseTaskHookInput parses PreToolUse[Task] hook input from reader
    46→func parseTaskHookInput(r io.Reader) (*TaskHookInput, error) {
    47→	data, err := io.ReadAll(r)
    48→	if err != nil {
    49→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read input: %w", err)
    50→	}
    51→
    52→	if len(data) == 0 {
    53→		return nil, errors.New("empty input")
    54→	}
    55→
    56→	var input TaskHookInput
    57→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &input); err != nil {
    58→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse JSON: %w", err)
    59→	}
    60→
    61→	return &input, nil
    62→}
    63→
    64→// parsePostTaskHookInput parses PostToolUse[Task] hook input from reader
    65→func parsePostTaskHookInput(r io.Reader) (*PostTaskHookInput, error) {
    66→	data, err := io.ReadAll(r)
    67→	if err != nil {
    68→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read input: %w", err)
    69→	}
    70→
    71→	if len(data) == 0 {
    72→		return nil, errors.New("empty input")
    73→	}
    74→
    75→	var raw postTaskHookInputRaw
    76→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
    77→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse JSON: %w", err)
    78→	}
    79→
    80→	return &PostTaskHookInput{
    81→		TaskHookInput: TaskHookInput{
    82→			SessionID:      raw.SessionID,
    83→			TranscriptPath: raw.TranscriptPath,
    84→			ToolUseID:      raw.ToolUseID,
    85→		},
    86→		AgentID:   raw.ToolResponse.AgentID,
    87→		ToolInput: raw.ToolInput,
    88→	}, nil
    89→}
    90→
    91→// logPreTaskHookContext logs the PreToolUse[Task] hook context to the writer
    92→func logPreTaskHookContext(w io.Writer, input *TaskHookInput) {
    93→	_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] PreToolUse[Task] hook invoked")
    94→	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Session ID: %s\n", input.SessionID)
    95→	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Tool Use ID: %s\n", input.ToolUseID)
    96→	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Transcript: %s\n", input.TranscriptPath)
    97→}

   108→}

   111→func parseSubagentCheckpointHookInput(r io.Reader) (*SubagentCheckpointHookInput, error) {
   112→	data, err := io.ReadAll(r)
   113→	if err != nil {

   115→	}
   116→

   129→// taskToolInput represents the tool_input structure for the Task tool.

   131→type taskToolInput struct {
   132→	SubagentType string `json:"subagent_type"`
   133→	Description  string `json:"description"`
   134→}
   135→
   136→// ParseSubagentTypeAndDescription extracts subagent_type and description from Task tool_input.
   137→// Returns empty strings if parsing fails or fields are not present.
   138→func ParseSubagentTypeAndDescription(toolInput json.RawMessage) (agentType, description string) {
   139→	if len(toolInput) == 0 {
   140→		return "", ""
   141→	}
   142→
   143→	var input taskToolInput
   144→	if err := json.Unmarshal(toolInput, &input); err != nil {
   145→		return "", ""
   146→	}
   147→
   148→	return input.SubagentType, input.Description
   149→}

   358→
   359→	// Verify B, C are back
   360→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_b.go"), "combo_b.go should be back after unstash")
   361→	assert.True(t, env.FileExists("combo_c.go"), "combo_c.go should be back after unstash")
   362→
   363→	// User commits ALL files together (B, C, D, E)
   364→	t.Log("Committing all remaining files together")
   365→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add combo_b, combo_c, combo_d, combo_e",
   366→		"combo_b.go", "combo_c.go", "combo_d.go", "combo_e.go")
   367→
   368→	// Verify checkpoint was created
   369→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   370→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 2, "Should have checkpoints")
   371→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   372→
   373→	// The second commit should have all 4 files linked to a single checkpoint
   374→	// Verify metadata branch exists
   375→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   376→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
   377→
   378→	// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts
   379→	// checkpointIDs[0] is the most recent (B, C, D, E combined commit)
   380→	// checkpointIDs[1] is the earlier commit (A only)
   381→	//
   382→	// Prompt 1 created A, B, C. User committed A, then stashed B, C.
   383→	// Prompt 2 created D, E. User unstashed B, C, then committed all 4 together.
   384→	if len(checkpointIDs) >= 2 {
   385→		// The BCDE commit happens during prompt 2's session, so its transcript
   386→		// contains prompt 2's work (D, E). B, C are included via carry-forward.
   387→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   388→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],
   389→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   390→			FilesTouched:              []string{"combo_b.go", "combo_c.go", "combo_d.go", "combo_e.go"},
   391→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"combo_d.go", "combo_e.go"}, // Prompt 2 transcript
   392→		})
   393→		// The A commit has full prompt 1 transcript (A, B, C were all created)
   394→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   395→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[1],
   396→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   397→			FilesTouched:              []string{"combo_a.go"},
   398→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"combo_a.go", "combo_b.go", "combo_c.go"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript
   399→		})
   400→	}
   401→}

   403→// TestE2E_Scenario7_PartialStagingWithGitAddP tests partial staging with git add -p.
   404→//
   405→// Scenario 7: Partial Staging with `git add -p`
   406→// - Agent makes multiple changes to a single file
   407→// - User stages only part of the changes (simulated with partial write)
   408→// - Content-aware carry-forward detects partial commit
   409→// - Remaining changes carried forward to next commit
   410→func TestE2E_Scenario7_PartialStagingSimulated(t *testing.T) {
   411→	t.Parallel()
   412→
   413→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   414→
   415→	// Agent creates a file with multiple functions
   416→	t.Log("Creating file with multiple functions")
   417→	multiLinePrompt := `Create a file called partial.go with this exact content:
   418→package main
   419→
   420→func First() int {
   421→	return 1
   422→}
   423→
   424→func Second() int {
   425→	return 2
   426→}
   427→
   428→func Third() int {
   429→	return 3
   430→}
   431→
   432→func Fourth() int {
   433→	return 4
   434→}
   435→
   436→Create only this file with exactly this content.`
   437→
   438→	result, err := env.RunAgent(multiLinePrompt)
   439→	require.NoError(t, err)
   440→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   441→
   442→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("partial.go"))
   443→
   444→	// Check rewind points before commit
   445→	pointsBefore := env.GetRewindPoints()
   446→	t.Logf("Rewind points before commit: %d", len(pointsBefore))
   447→
   448→	// Simulate partial staging by temporarily replacing file with partial content
   449→	// Save the full content
   450→	fullContent := env.ReadFile("partial.go")
   451→	t.Logf("Full content length: %d bytes", len(fullContent))
   452→
   453→	// Write partial content (only first two functions)
   454→	partialContent := `package main
   455→
   456→func First() int {
   457→	return 1
   458→}
   459→
   460→func Second() int {
   461→	return 2
   462→}
   463→`
   464→	env.WriteFile("partial.go", partialContent)
   465→
   466→	// Commit the partial content
   467→	t.Log("Committing partial content (First and Second functions)")
   468→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add first two functions", "partial.go")
   469→
   470→	// Verify first checkpoint was created
   471→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   472→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDs), 1, "Should have first checkpoint")
   473→	t.Logf("First checkpoint ID: %s", checkpointIDs[0])
   474→
   475→	// Restore the full content (simulating remaining changes still in worktree)
   476→	env.WriteFile("partial.go", fullContent)
   477→
   478→	// Commit the remaining content
   479→	t.Log("Committing full content (all functions)")
   480→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add remaining functions", "partial.go")
   481→
   482→	// Verify second checkpoint was created
   483→	checkpointIDsAfter := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   484→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfter), 2, "Should have two checkpoints")
   485→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDsAfter)
   486→
   487→	// Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID
   488→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointIDsAfter[0], checkpointIDsAfter[1],
   489→		"Each commit should have its own unique checkpoint ID")
   490→
   491→	// Validate checkpoints have proper metadata and transcripts
   492→	// checkpointIDsAfter[0] is the most recent (full content commit)
   493→	// checkpointIDsAfter[1] is the earlier commit (partial content)
   494→	//
   495→	// Both commits are from the same session (single prompt), so both have
   496→	// the same full transcript referencing partial.go and the function names.
   497→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   498→		CheckpointID:              checkpointIDsAfter[0],
   499→		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   500→		FilesTouched:              []string{"partial.go"},
   501→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"partial.go", "First", "Second", "Third", "Fourth"},
   502→	})
   503→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   504→		CheckpointID:              checkpointIDsAfter[1],
   505→		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   506→		FilesTouched:              []string{"partial.go"},
   507→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"partial.go", "First", "Second", "Third", "Fourth"},
   508→	})
   509→}

   511→// TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace tests content-aware overlap detection
   512→// when user reverts session changes and writes different content.
   513→//
   514→// Content-Aware Overlap Detection:
   515→// - Agent creates file X with content "hello"
   516→// - User reverts X (git checkout -- X)
   517→// - User writes completely different content
   518→// - User commits
   519→// - Content mismatch → NO checkpoint trailer added
   520→func TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace(t *testing.T) {
   521→	t.Parallel()
   522→
   523→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   524→
   525→	// Agent creates a file
   526→	t.Log("Agent creating file with specific content")
   527→	createPrompt := `Create a file called overlap_test.go with this exact content:
   528→package main
   529→
   530→func OverlapOriginal() string {
   531→	return "original content from agent"
   532→}
   533→
   534→Create only this file.`
   535→
   536→	result, err := env.RunAgent(createPrompt)
   537→	require.NoError(t, err)
   538→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   539→
   540→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("overlap_test.go"))
   541→	originalContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   542→	t.Logf("Original content: %s", originalContent)
   543→
   544→	// Verify rewind points exist (session tracked the change)
   545→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   546→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind points")
   547→
   548→	// User reverts the file and writes completely different content
   549→	t.Log("User reverting file and writing different content")
   550→	differentContent := `package main
   551→
   552→func CompletelyDifferent() string {
   553→	return "user wrote this, not the agent"
   554→}
   555→`
   556→	env.WriteFile("overlap_test.go", differentContent)
   557→
   558→	// Verify content is different
   559→	currentContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   560→	assert.NotEqual(t, originalContent, currentContent)
   561→
   562→	// Commits before this test
   563→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
   564→
   565→	// User commits the different content
   566→	t.Log("Committing user-written content")
   567→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add overlap test file", "overlap_test.go")
   568→
   569→	// Verify commit was made
   570→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
   571→	assert.Equal(t, commitsBefore+1, commitsAfter, "Should have one new commit")
   572→
   573→	// Check for checkpoint trailer
   574→	// With content-aware overlap detection, if the user completely replaced
   575→	// the agent's content (new file with different hash), there should be
   576→	// NO checkpoint trailer added. This is documented in checkpoint-scenarios.md
   577→	// under "Content-Aware Overlap Detection".
   578→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   579→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs found: %v", checkpointIDs)
   580→
   581→	// The first commit (Initial commit from NewFeatureBranchEnv) doesn't have a checkpoint.
   582→	// Only agent-assisted commits should have checkpoint trailers.
   583→	// When user completely replaces agent content, content-aware detection should
   584→	// prevent the checkpoint trailer from being added.
   585→	//
   586→	// Per docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md:
   587→	// - New file + content hash mismatch → No overlap → No checkpoint trailer
   588→	assert.Empty(t, checkpointIDs,
   589→		"Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint trailer when user completely replaces agent content")
   590→}

   592→// TestE2E_Scenario1_BasicFlow verifies the simplest workflow matches the documented scenario.
   593→//
   594→// Scenario 1: Prompt → Changes → Prompt Finishes → User Commits
   595→// This test explicitly verifies the documented flow.
   596→func TestE2E_Scenario1_BasicFlow(t *testing.T) {
   597→	t.Parallel()
   598→
   599→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   600→
   601→	// 1. User submits prompt (triggers UserPromptSubmit hook → InitializeSession)
   602→	t.Log("Step 1: User submits prompt")
   603→
   604→	// 2. Claude makes changes (creates files)
   605→	prompt := `Create a file called scenario1.go with this content:
   606→package main
   607→func Scenario1() {}
   608→Create only this file.`
   609→
   610→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   611→	require.NoError(t, err)
   612→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   613→
   614→	// Verify file was created
   615→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("scenario1.go"))
   616→
   617→	// 3. After stop hook: checkpoint is saved, FilesTouched is set
   618→	t.Log("Step 3: Checking rewind points after stop")
   619→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   620→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind point after stop")
   621→	t.Logf("Rewind points: %d", len(points))
   622→
   623→	// 4. User commits (triggers prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks)
   624→	t.Log("Step 4: User commits")
   625→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add scenario1 file", "scenario1.go")
   626→
   627→	// 5. Verify checkpoint was created with trailer
   628→	checkpointID, err := env.GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory()
   629→	require.NoError(t, err, "Should find checkpoint in commit history")
   630→	assert.NotEmpty(t, checkpointID, "Commit should have Entire-Checkpoint trailer")
   631→	t.Logf("Checkpoint ID: %s", checkpointID)
   632→
   633→	// 6. Verify shadow branch was cleaned up and metadata branch exists
   634→	assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   635→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist after condensation")
   636→
   637→	// 7. Validate checkpoint has proper metadata and transcript
   638→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   639→		CheckpointID:              checkpointID,
   640→		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   641→		FilesTouched:              []string{"scenario1.go"},
   642→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"scenario1.go"},
   643→	})
   644→}

   646→// TestE2E_Scenario2_AgentCommitsDuringTurn verifies the deferred finalization flow.
   647→//
   648→// Scenario 2: Prompt Commits Within Single Turn
   649→// - Agent commits during ACTIVE phase
   650→// - PostCommit saves provisional transcript
   651→// - HandleTurnEnd (Stop hook) finalizes with full transcript
   652→func TestE2E_Scenario2_AgentCommitsDuringTurn(t *testing.T) {
   653→	t.Parallel()
   654→
   655→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   656→
   657→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
   658→
   659→	// Agent creates file and commits it
   660→	t.Log("Agent creating file and committing")
   661→	commitPrompt := `Create a file called agent_commit.go with this content:
   662→package main
   663→func AgentCommit() {}
   664→
   665→Then commit it with: git add agent_commit.go && git commit -m "Agent adds file"
   666→
   667→Create the file first, then run the git commands.`
   668→
   669→	result, err := env.RunAgentWithTools(commitPrompt, []string{"Write", "Bash"})
   670→	require.NoError(t, err)
   671→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   672→
   673→	// Verify file was created
   674→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("agent_commit.go"))
   675→
   676→	// Verify commit was made
   677→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
   678→	assert.Greater(t, commitsAfter, commitsBefore, "Agent should have made a commit")
   679→
   680→	// Check commit message
   681→	headMsg := env.GetCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
   682→	t.Logf("HEAD commit message: %s", headMsg)
   683→
   684→	// Check for checkpoint trailer
   685→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   686→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   687→
   688→	// Verify metadata branch exists (if checkpoint was created)
   689→	if len(checkpointIDs) > 0 {
   690→		assert.True(t, env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1"),
   691→			"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist")
   692→
   693→		// Validate checkpoint has proper metadata and transcript
   694→		env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   695→			CheckpointID:              checkpointIDs[0],
   696→			Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
   697→			FilesTouched:              []string{"agent_commit.go"},
   698→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"agent_commit.go"},
   699→		})
   700→	}
   701→}

   703→// =============================================================================
   704→// Tests for MODIFYING EXISTING FILES (not just creating new ones)
   705→// =============================================================================
   706→// These tests ensure checkpoints work correctly when the agent modifies
   707→// tracked files that already exist in the repository, which behaves differently
   708→// from creating new (untracked) files with respect to git stash, staging, etc.
   709→
   710→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_ModifyAndCommit tests basic workflow where agent
   711→// modifies an existing tracked file instead of creating a new one.
   712→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_ModifyAndCommit(t *testing.T) {
   713→	t.Parallel()
   714→
   715→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   716→
   717→	// Create and commit an existing file first
   718→	env.WriteFile("config.go", `package main
   719→
   720→var Config = map[string]string{
   721→	"version": "1.0",
   722→}
   723→`)
   724→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add initial config", "config.go")
   725→
   726→	// Agent modifies the existing file
   727→	t.Log("Agent modifying existing config.go")
   728→	prompt := `Modify the file config.go to add a new config key "debug" with value "true".
   729→Keep the existing content and just add the new key. Only modify this one file.`
   730→
   731→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   732→	require.NoError(t, err)
   733→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   734→
   735→	// Verify file was modified
   736→	content := env.ReadFile("config.go")
   737→	assert.Contains(t, content, "debug", "config.go should contain debug key")
   738→
   739→	// User commits the modification
   740→	t.Log("User committing modified config.go")
   741→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add debug config", "config.go")
   742→
   743→	// Verify checkpoint was created
   744→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   745→	// First commit (initial config) may or may not have checkpoint depending on session state
   746→	// The agent's modification commit should have a checkpoint
   747→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpointIDs, "Should have at least one checkpoint")
   748→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   749→}
   750→
   751→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications tests stashing modifications to
   752→// tracked files (not new untracked files). This exercises the standard git stash
   753→// behavior (without -u flag) since modifications to tracked files are stashable.
   754→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications(t *testing.T) {
   755→	t.Parallel()
   756→
   757→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   758→
   759→	// Create and commit two existing files
   760→	env.WriteFile("fileA.go", "package main\n\nfunc A() { /* original */ }\n")
   761→	env.WriteFile("fileB.go", "package main\n\nfunc B() { /* original */ }\n")
   762→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add initial files", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   763→
   764→	// Agent modifies both files
   765→	t.Log("Agent modifying fileA.go and fileB.go")
   766→	prompt := `Modify these files:
   767→1. In fileA.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   768→2. In fileB.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   769→Only modify these two files.`
   770→
   771→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   772→	require.NoError(t, err)
   773→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   774→
   775→	// Verify both files were modified
   776→	contentA := env.ReadFile("fileA.go")
   777→	contentB := env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   778→	assert.Contains(t, contentA, "modified by agent", "fileA.go should be modified")
   779→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should be modified")
   780→
   781→	// User commits only fileA.go
   782→	t.Log("Committing only fileA.go")
   783→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileA", "fileA.go")
   784→	checkpoint1 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   785→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint1, "First commit should have checkpoint")
   786→
   787→	// User stashes fileB.go modifications (tracked file, standard stash works)
   788→	t.Log("Stashing fileB.go modifications")
   789→	env.GitStash()
   790→
   791→	// Verify fileB.go is reverted to original
   792→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   793→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "original", "fileB.go should be reverted after stash")
   794→	assert.NotContains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should not have agent changes")
   795→
   796→	// User pops the stash and commits fileB.go
   797→	t.Log("Popping stash and committing fileB.go")
   798→	env.GitStashPop()
   799→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   800→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should have agent changes after stash pop")
   801→
   802→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileB", "fileB.go")
   803→	checkpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   804→
   805→	// Both commits should have checkpoints
   806→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, "Second commit should have checkpoint")
   807→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, "Checkpoints should be different")
   808→
   809→	t.Logf("Checkpoint 1: %s, Checkpoint 2: %s", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)
   810→}

   812→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits tests user splitting agent's modifications
   813→// to multiple existing files into separate commits.
   814→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits(t *testing.T) {
   815→	t.Parallel()
   816→
   817→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   818→
   819→	// Create and commit multiple existing files
   820→	env.WriteFile("model.go", "package main\n\ntype Model struct{}\n")
   821→	env.WriteFile("view.go", "package main\n\ntype View struct{}\n")
   822→	env.WriteFile("controller.go", "package main\n\ntype Controller struct{}\n")
   823→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add MVC scaffolding", "model.go", "view.go", "controller.go")
   824→
   825→	// Agent modifies all three files
   826→	t.Log("Agent modifying model.go, view.go, controller.go")
   827→	prompt := `Add a Name field (string type) to each struct in these files:
   828→1. model.go - add Name string to Model struct
   829→2. view.go - add Name string to View struct
   830→3. controller.go - add Name string to Controller struct
   831→Only modify these three files.`
   832→
   833→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   834→	require.NoError(t, err)
   835→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   836→
   837→	// User commits each file separately
   838→	t.Log("Committing model.go")
   839→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add Name to Model", "model.go")
   840→	checkpointModel := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   841→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpointModel, "Model commit should have checkpoint")
   842→
   843→	t.Log("Committing view.go")
   844→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add Name to View", "view.go")
   845→	checkpointView := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   846→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpointView, "View commit should have checkpoint")
   847→
   848→	t.Log("Committing controller.go")
   849→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add Name to Controller", "controller.go")
   850→	checkpointController := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   851→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpointController, "Controller commit should have checkpoint")
   852→
   853→	// All three checkpoints should be different
   854→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointModel, checkpointView)
   855→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointView, checkpointController)
   856→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpointModel, checkpointController)
   857→
   858→	t.Logf("Checkpoints: model=%s, view=%s, controller=%s",
   859→		checkpointModel, checkpointView, checkpointController)
   860→
   861→	// Validate each checkpoint has the correct files_touched
   862→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   863→		CheckpointID: checkpointModel,
   864→		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
   865→		FilesTouched: []string{"model.go"},
   866→	})
   867→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   868→		CheckpointID: checkpointView,
   869→		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
   870→		FilesTouched: []string{"view.go"},
   871→	})
   872→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   873→		CheckpointID: checkpointController,
   874→		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
   875→		FilesTouched: []string{"controller.go"},
   876→	})
   877→}

   879→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification tests that modifying an existing file
   880→// that was touched by the session ALWAYS gets a checkpoint, even if the user writes
   881→// completely different content.
   882→//
   883→// This is intentional behavior: for files that already exist in HEAD (modified files),
   884→// we always count as overlap because the user is editing a file the session worked on.
   885→// Content-aware detection only applies to NEW files (don't exist in HEAD).
   886→//
   887→// See content_overlap.go for the rationale.
   888→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification(t *testing.T) {
   889→	t.Parallel()
   890→
   891→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   892→
   893→	// Create and commit an existing file
   894→	originalContent := `package main
   895→
   896→// placeholder
   897→`
   898→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", originalContent)
   899→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add placeholder", "calc.go")
   900→
   901→	// Agent modifies the existing file
   902→	t.Log("Agent modifying calc.go")
   903→	prompt := `Replace the contents of calc.go with this exact code:
   904→package main
   905→
   906→func AgentMultiply(a, b int) int {
   907→	return a * b
   908→}
   909→
   910→Only modify calc.go, nothing else.`
   911→
   912→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   913→	require.NoError(t, err)
   914→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   915→
   916→	// Verify agent modified the file
   917→	modifiedContent := env.ReadFile("calc.go")
   918→	assert.Contains(t, modifiedContent, "AgentMultiply", "calc.go should have AgentMultiply function")
   919→
   920→	// User reverts and writes completely different content
   921→	t.Log("User reverting and writing completely different content")
   922→	userContent := `package main
   923→
   924→func UserAdd(x, y int) int {
   925→	return x + y
   926→}
   927→`
   928→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", userContent)
   929→
   930→	// User commits their changes
   931→	t.Log("Committing user's changes")
   932→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add user functions", "calc.go")
   933→
   934→	// For MODIFIED files (existing in HEAD), we always count as overlap.
   935→	// The checkpoint SHOULD be created even though content is different.
   936→	// This is because the session touched this file, so any commit to it
   937→	// should be linked to preserve the editing history.
   938→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   939→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   940→
   941→	latestCheckpoint := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   942→	assert.NotEmpty(t, latestCheckpoint,
   943→		"Modified files should always get checkpoint (content-aware only applies to new files)")
   944→}
   945→
   946→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified tests a scenario where the agent
   947→// both creates new files AND modifies existing files in the same session.
   948→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified(t *testing.T) {
   949→	t.Parallel()
   950→
   951→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   952→
   953→	// Create and commit an existing file
   954→	env.WriteFile("main.go", `package main
   955→
   956→func main() {
   957→	// TODO: add imports
   958→}
   959→`)
   960→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add main.go", "main.go")
   961→
   962→	// Agent modifies existing file AND creates new files
   963→	t.Log("Agent modifying main.go and creating new files")
   964→	prompt := `Do these tasks:
   965→1. Create a new file utils.go with: package main; func Helper() string { return "helper" }
   966→2. Create a new file types.go with: package main; type Config struct { Name string }
   967→3. Modify main.go to add a comment "// imports utils and types" at the top (after package main)
   968→Complete all three tasks.`
   969→
   970→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   971→	require.NoError(t, err)
   972→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   973→
   974→	// Verify all changes
   975→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("utils.go"), "utils.go should exist")
   976→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("types.go"), "types.go should exist")
   977→	mainContent := env.ReadFile("main.go")
   978→	assert.Contains(t, mainContent, "imports utils and types", "main.go should be modified")
   979→
   980→	// User commits existing file modification first
   981→	t.Log("Committing main.go modification")
   982→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update main.go imports comment", "main.go")
   983→	checkpoint1 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   984→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint1, "main.go commit should have checkpoint")
   985→
   986→	// User commits new files together
   987→	t.Log("Committing new files utils.go and types.go")
   988→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add utils and types", "utils.go", "types.go")
   989→	checkpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   990→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, "New files commit should have checkpoint")
   991→
   992→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, "Checkpoints should be different")
   993→	t.Logf("Checkpoint 1 (modified): %s, Checkpoint 2 (new): %s", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)
   994→}

   151→func (r *ClaudeCodeRunner) RunPromptWithTools(ctx context.Context, workDir string, prompt string, tools []string) (*AgentResult, error) {
   152→	// Build command: claude --model <model> -p "<prompt>" --allowedTools <tools>
   153→	args := []string{
   154→		"--model", r.Model,
   155→		"-p", prompt,
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	if len(tools) > 0 {
   159→		// Claude CLI expects each tool as a separate argument after --allowedTools
   160→		// e.g., --allowedTools Edit Read Bash (not --allowedTools "Edit,Read,Bash")
   161→		args = append(args, "--allowedTools")
   162→		args = append(args, tools...)
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Create context with timeout
   166→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.Timeout)
   167→	defer cancel()
   168→
   169→	//nolint:gosec // args are constructed from trusted config, not user input
   170→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude", args...)
   171→	cmd.Dir = workDir
   172→
   173→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   174→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   175→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   176→
   177→	start := time.Now()
   178→	err := cmd.Run()
   179→	duration := time.Since(start)
   180→
   181→	result := &AgentResult{
   182→		Stdout:   stdout.String(),
   183→		Stderr:   stderr.String(),
   184→		Duration: duration,
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	if err != nil {
   188→		exitErr := &exec.ExitError{}
   189→		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   190→			result.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
   191→		} else {
   192→			result.ExitCode = -1
   193→		}
   194→		//nolint:wrapcheck // error is from exec.Run, caller can check ExitCode in result
   195→		return result, err
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	result.ExitCode = 0
   199→	return result, nil
   200→}
